definition_zh: 无脊椎动物；无脊椎的
definition_en: an animal without a backbone, or lacking a backbone
core_image: 退潮的水洼里，一团没有骨架的软体摊在石上，靠水支撑着形状
scene: 退潮后的水洼里，一只没有骨架的软体动物摊在石头上，靠残留的水维持形状。 Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on the water to hold its shape.
sceneCN: 这里 invertebrate 指「无脊椎动物」（第 1 个义项：没有脊柱的动物）；句意为由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物只能靠水来维持体形。

derivatives.zh: 无脊椎动物类群（旧分类名）

senses.title: An animal without a backbone
senses.definition: any animal that lacks a vertebral column, including insects, worms, mollusks and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 任何没有脊柱的动物，包括昆虫、蠕虫、软体动物与甲壳动物
senses.example: Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on water to hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物靠水维持体形。
senses.why: The word is literally 'without vertebrae': in- 'not' plus vertebra, the bones of the spine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「没有脊椎」：in-「不」加 vertebra（脊柱的骨节）。

senses.title: The adjective: lacking a backbone
senses.definition: describing an animal or body plan that has no spinal column
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有脊柱的动物或身体结构
senses.example: The invertebrate body plan allows bending in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎的身体结构允许向各个方向弯曲。
senses.why: English uses the same form for noun and adjective, so the ending -ate does double duty.
senses.whyCN: 英语中名词与形容词同形，因此 -ate 词尾同时承担两种功能。

senses.title: The field of invertebrate zoology
senses.titleCN: 无脊椎动物学这一学科
senses.definition: the branch of zoology that studies animals without backbones
senses.definitionCN: 研究无脊柱动物的动物学分支
senses.example: Invertebrate zoology covers far more species than vertebrate zoology.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎动物学涵盖的物种远多于脊椎动物学。
senses.why: Because most animal species lack a backbone, the adjective became a discipline label.
senses.whyCN: 由于大多数动物物种没有脊柱，这个形容词成了一个学科标签。

senses.title: A fossil invertebrate
senses.definition: ancient remains of an animal without a backbone, often shells or exoskeletons
senses.definitionCN: 无脊柱动物的古代遗骸，常为贝壳或外骨骼
senses.example: The oldest invertebrate fossils are more than half a billion years old.
senses.exampleCN: 最古老的无脊椎动物化石已有五亿多年历史。
senses.why: Hard shells and exoskeletons preserve far better than soft vertebrate tissue, so the fossil record is dominated by invertebrates.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳与外骨骼比脊椎动物的软组织更易保存，因此化石记录以无脊椎动物为主。

senses.title: A marine invertebrate
senses.definition: an invertebrate living in the sea, such as a coral, crab or sea worm
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的无脊椎动物，如珊瑚、蟹或海虫
senses.example: Marine invertebrates build most of the reef structure.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋无脊椎动物建造了大部分礁体结构。
senses.why: Ecology uses the category because reef builders and sea-floor communities cross many phyla.
senses.whyCN: 生态学使用这一范畴，因为造礁者与海底群落跨越许多门。

senses.title: A source of food and stock
senses.definition: an invertebrate harvested or farmed for food, such as shrimp, squid or oysters
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞或养殖的无脊椎动物，如虾、鱿鱼或牡蛎
senses.example: Most aquaculture production is invertebrate.
senses.exampleCN: 水产养殖的大部分产量来自无脊椎动物。
senses.why: The category groups together very different edible animals that share only the absence of a spine.
senses.whyCN: 这一范畴把差异极大、只共享「没有脊柱」这一点的可食动物归在一起。

senses.title: Figurative: lacking firmness or courage
senses.definition: describing a person or organization seen as weak-willed or lacking firm principles
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人或组织意志软弱、缺乏坚定原则
senses.example: Critics called the committee invertebrate for postponing the decision again.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说委员会又一次推迟决定，毫无骨气。
senses.why: The metaphor takes 'no backbone' from anatomy and applies it to character: no spine, no resolve.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把解剖上的「没有脊柱」用到性格上：没有脊梁，就没有决断。

senses.title: A bioindicator community
senses.definition: invertebrates used to assess water or soil quality because they respond quickly to pollution
senses.definitionCN: 因对污染反应迅速而被用来评估水或土壤质量的无脊椎动物
senses.example: Stream invertebrates are sampled to grade water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 通过采样溪流无脊椎动物来评定水质。
senses.why: Monitoring programs use the category because mayflies, snails and worms together signal different pollution levels.
senses.whyCN: 监测项目使用这一范畴，因为蜉蝣、螺与蠕虫共同指示不同的污染水平。

intro.en: Invertebrate is Latin in- 'not' plus vertebra 'joint of the spine', with the adjective ending -ate; the word is a modern scientific formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: invertebrate 由拉丁 in-「不」加 vertebra「脊柱的骨节」，再加形容词词尾 -ate 构成；它是近代科学造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertebra meant a joint, especially a joint of the spine, from vertere 'to turn'. The link to 'turn' is generally accepted; the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: vertebra 意为「关节」，尤指脊柱的关节，来自 vertere「转动」。与「转动」的联系一般被接受；更深的词根属重构。

items.en: The prefix in- 'not' negates the noun, so an invertebrate is literally 'one without vertebrae'.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「不」否定该名词，因此 invertebrate 字面就是「没有脊椎的东西」。

items.en: Lamarck's early nineteenth-century classification used invertébrés for animals without a spinal column, and English borrowed the term.
items.cn: 拉马克在 19 世纪初的分类中使用 invertébrés 指没有脊柱的动物，英语借入了这个词。

items.en: English invertebrate appears in the nineteenth century as both noun and adjective, in zoology and in general prose.
items.cn: 英语 invertebrate 在 19 世纪出现，既作名词也作形容词，见于动物学与一般散文。

items.en: By the later nineteenth century 'no backbone' was applied to people and institutions lacking firmness, and the figurative sense entered dictionaries.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪后期，「没有脊梁」被用于形容缺乏坚定性的人与机构，比喻义进入词典。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin root of vertere is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 vertere 的拉丁语之前词根属重构，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same vertebra stock that are easily confused; group two holds animal-category words that overlap with invertebrate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vertebra 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是与无脊椎动物重叠的动物范畴词。

entries.definition: An animal with a backbone; it differs from invertebrate by the single negative prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 有脊柱的动物；与 invertebrate 只差一个否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: A single bone of the spine; several are vertebrae. The animal word is built on this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 脊柱的一块骨；多块为 vertebrae。动物词正是在这个名词上构成的。

entries.definition: Relating to a vertebra or the spine, as in vertebral column; it is not the animal category word.
entries.definitionCN: 与椎骨或脊柱有关，如 vertebral column；它不是动物类别词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to turn upside down, from in- + vertere 'turn'; it shares the root but is not related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为翻转，由 in- + vertere「转」构成；同词根，但意义无关。

entries.definition: A jointed-legged invertebrate; arthropods are the largest subgroup of invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；节肢动物是最大的无脊椎动物亚群。

entries.definition: A soft-bodied invertebrate, usually with a shell; another subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物；另一个亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A segmented worm such as an earthworm; it is one kind of invertebrate among very many.
entries.definitionCN: 分节的蠕虫，如蚯蚓；它是众多无脊椎动物中的一类。

entries.definition: Small drifting animals in water, many of them invertebrates; the term names a lifestyle, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 水中漂浮的小型动物，许多是无脊椎动物；这个词命名生活方式，而不是类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'not' + vertebrate 'backboned': the animal with no spine.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ vertebrate「有脊椎的」：没有脊柱的动物。

normal.en: Vertebra is one spinal bone; vertebrae are several; invertebrate means none at all.
normal.cn: vertebra 是一块椎骨，vertebrae 是多块，invertebrate 则一块也没有。

normal.en: Most animal species are invertebrates: insects alone outnumber all vertebrates.
normal.cn: 大多数动物物种是无脊椎动物：仅昆虫就超过所有脊椎动物。

normal.en: The figurative use is 'no backbone' in character, not in anatomy.
normal.cn: 比喻义指性格上「没有脊梁」，而非解剖结构。

normal.en: Invertebrate zoology is a field name, because the category covers dozens of phyla.
normal.cn: invertebrate zoology 是学科名，因为这一范畴涵盖数十个门。

abstract.en: Picture a body that holds itself up with water instead of bone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用水的力量而不是骨头来支撑的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a committee with no spine, bending whichever way the wind blows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有脊梁的委员会，风往哪吹就往哪倒。

abstract.en: Picture a mayfly in a stream acting as a tiny water-quality meter.
abstract.cn: 想象溪流里一只蜉蝣，充当一枚微小的水质计。

examples.en: Invertebrates make up roughly ninety-five per cent of animal species.
examples.cn: 无脊椎动物约占动物物种的百分之九十五。

examples.en: The survey recorded invertebrates but no vertebrates in the polluted stream.
examples.cn: 调查在被污染的溪流中记录到无脊椎动物，却没有脊椎动物。

examples.en: The minister was called invertebrate for refusing to defend the policy.
examples.cn: 这位部长因拒绝为该政策辩护而被称为没有骨气。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vertebrate（有脊椎的）——没有脊椎的动物；记「软体、虫、虾蟹都不靠脊梁」

root: 拉丁 in-「不」+ vertebra「脊椎骨节」（源自 vertere「转动」）+ -ate；vertebra 的更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one negative fact, the absence of a spine, through zoology, palaeontology, ecology, fisheries, metaphor and pollution monitoring.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕一个否定事实——没有脊柱，穿过动物学、古生物学、生态学、渔业、比喻与污染监测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft body in a tide pool, held up by water rather than bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里一具柔软的身体，靠水而非骨骼支撑。

branches.en: ABSENCE: noun and adjective both say the same thing, that there is no vertebral column.
branches.cn: 缺失：名词与形容词说的是同一件事——没有脊柱。

branches.en: A FIELD: because the category is so wide, it becomes a branch of zoology.
branches.cn: 一个学科：范畴太宽，于是成了一门动物学分支。

branches.en: HARD PARTS IN SOFT ANIMALS: shells and exoskeletons dominate the fossil and reef records.
branches.cn: 软体中的硬部件：贝壳与外骨骼主导了化石与礁体记录。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND INSTRUMENT: food from the sea, and a meter for its health.
branches.cn: 资源与仪器：既是海中食物，也是衡量其健康的仪表。

branches.en: METAPHOR: no spine becomes no courage.
branches.cn: 比喻：没有脊柱变成了没有骨气。

intro.en: Invertebrate is a prefixed derivative of vertebra, so its parts are a negative prefix, a noun and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: invertebrate 是 vertebra 的加缀派生词，其成分是否定前缀、名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertebra comes from vertere 'to turn'; in- negates it, and -atus supplies the adjective shape that English reduced to -ate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertebra 来自 vertere「转动」；in- 加以否定，-atus 提供形容词形态，英语简化为 -ate。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定了脊柱的存在。

items.example: Each vertebra turns slightly on the next.
items.exampleCN: 每块椎骨都能相对下一块略微转动。

items.example: The ending makes the word an adjective as well as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使该词兼作形容词与名词。

items.example: The invertebrate has no spinal column.
items.exampleCN: 这只无脊椎动物没有脊柱。

items.example: Vertebrates are the minority of animal species.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物只占动物物种的少数。

items.example: The vertebral column protects the nerve cord.
Invert shares the turning root but not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: invert 同出「转」词根，但意义不同。

definition_zh: 面容；表情；镇定；支持；容许
definition_en: a person's face or expression, composure, or the act of giving support and approval
core_image: 一张在喧闹中仍不变形的脸，眉目平直，像被端平的一碗水
scene: 宣布结果时，她的脸上没有一丝波动，等所有人离开才松一口气。 She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
sceneCN: 这里 countenance 指在压力下维持镇定的神色（第 2 个义项：镇定）；句意为宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。

senses.title: The face itself
senses.definition: a person's face, especially as it shows character
senses.definitionCN: 人的脸，尤指显露性格的面容
senses.example: A familiar countenance appeared at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口出现了一张熟悉的面容。
senses.why: The word came from Latin for 'containment': the face is the container that holds and shows the inner person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语「容纳」：脸是容纳并显示内在之人的容器。

senses.title: Composure under pressure
senses.definition: calm control of the face and feelings when others are watching
senses.definitionCN: 在他人注视下对面部与情绪的冷静控制
senses.example: She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。
senses.why: If the face is a container, composure is the lid staying on when the contents are under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 如果脸是容器，镇定就是内容物受压时盖子仍然盖住。

senses.title: Expression of a feeling
senses.definition: the look on a face that reveals a mood
senses.definitionCN: 脸上显露情绪的神情
senses.example: His countenance changed when he heard the price.
senses.exampleCN: 听到价格时他的表情变了。
senses.why: An expression is what leaks out of the container; the same face can hold a mood or reveal it.
senses.whyCN: 表情是从容器里漏出来的东西；同一张脸可以藏住情绪，也可以显露它。

senses.title: Support or approval
senses.definition: the act of giving approval or moral backing to something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某事物认可或道义支持的行为
senses.example: The board gave its countenance to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会支持这项合并。
senses.why: To lend one's face to a plan is to let the plan appear under one's name, which is what approval means.
senses.whyCN: 把脸借给一项计划，就是让计划以自己的名义出现，这正是批准的含义。

senses.title: Permission or tolerance
senses.definition: to allow something to happen without condemning it
senses.definitionCN: 允许某事发生而不加谴责
senses.example: The school would not countenance cheating.
senses.exampleCN: 学校不会容许作弊。
senses.why: Approval and tolerance differ in degree: the same face can back a plan or simply refuse to forbid it.
senses.whyCN: 批准与容忍只差程度：同一张脸既可以支持一项计划，也可以只是拒绝禁止它。

senses.title: Appearance or bearing
senses.definition: a person's general appearance and manner of carrying themselves
senses.definitionCN: 一个人总体的外观与举止方式
senses.example: He had the countenance of a man used to being obeyed.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一副惯于被服从的人的仪态。
senses.why: Bearing is the whole body's version of the face: how a person occupies space announces what the face only hints at.
senses.whyCN: 仪态是整副身体版本的面容：一个人如何占据空间，宣告了脸只暗示的东西。

senses.title: Moral backing
senses.definition: support that gives something respectability rather than money
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物获得体面地位而非金钱的支持
senses.example: The judge's presence lent countenance to the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的到场为调查增添了道义支持。
senses.why: Respectability is borrowed from someone whose face carries weight, so presence itself becomes a form of funding.
senses.whyCN: 体面是从一张有分量的脸上借来的，于是到场本身成了一种资助。

senses.title: Calm face in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, a calm and steady facial appearance
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，平静而稳定的面部外观
senses.example: The chronicle praises the queen's untroubled countenance.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称赞女王平静无扰的面色。
senses.why: Old writing used the word for an achieved stillness of face, the visible proof of an ordered inner life.
senses.whyCN: 较早的文本用这个词指一种修得的脸上静止，是内在秩序可见的证据。

intro.en: Countenance comes from a Latin verb meaning to contain or hold, and the face was understood as what holds the self.
intro.cn: countenance 来自一个意为「容纳、保持」的拉丁动词，脸被理解为容纳自我的容器。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the 13c. for the face and its expression, and the verb later meant to support.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个名词，指脸与表情；动词后来表示支持。

items.en: Continentia meant 'a holding together, self-control', from continere 'to hold together'.
items.cn: continentia 意为「保持一体、自我控制」，来自 continere「保持在一起」。

items.en: Continere 'to hold together, contain' is com- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: continere「保持、容纳」由 com-「一起」与 tenere「握住」构成。

items.en: Tenere 'to hold' also gives tenant, retain and contain, all built on keeping something in place.
items.cn: tenere「握住」也产生 tenant、retain 与 contain，都建立在「使某物留在原处」。

items.en: From the face that holds composure came the verb meaning to support or tolerate: to hold something up in public.
items.cn: 从「保持镇定的脸」发展出表示支持或容许的动词：在公开场合把某物托住。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the containing root; the near-meaning group names faces, calmness and approval.
note.cn: 形近组共享「容纳」词根；近义组列出面容、镇定与支持。

entries.definition: supported or tolerated in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 过去得到支持或容许的。

entries.definition: self-restraint, especially over the body.
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制，尤指对身体的克制。

entries.definition: to hold something inside.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物容纳在内。

entries.definition: the quality of holding oneself in check.
entries.definitionCN: 自我约束的性质。

entries.definition: the front of the head.
entries.definitionCN: 头的前部。

entries.definition: the look on a face that shows feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 脸上显示情感的神情。

entries.definition: calm control of one's feelings and appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 对情绪与外表的冷静控制。

entries.definition: a favourable opinion or official consent.
entries.definitionCN: 赞成的意见或正式同意。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the word to a face holding itself steady.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和「一张端住自己的脸」连起来。

normal.en: Think of contain: the face is a container that holds the self in.
normal.cn: 想想 contain：脸是容纳自我的容器。

normal.en: A countenance kept is a lid kept on under pressure.
normal.cn: 保持 countenance，就是压力下盖住盖子。

normal.en: To give countenance to a plan is to let it appear under your face.
normal.cn: 给某项计划 countenance，就是让它以你的面孔出现。

normal.en: Say coun-TEN-ance, with the holding root stressed.
normal.cn: 读成 coun-TEN-ance，重音落在表示「握住」的词根上。

normal.en: Link it with composure: both describe a face that does not spill.
normal.cn: 把它和 composure 联系：两者都描述不外泄的脸。

abstract.en: The face is the smallest public surface of the self.
abstract.cn: 脸是自我最小的公共表面。

abstract.en: Support and tolerance are the same gesture at different strengths.
abstract.cn: 支持与容许是同一姿态的不同强度。

abstract.en: A calm face can be honesty or a lid; the word does not decide.
abstract.cn: 平静的脸可以是诚实，也可以是一个盖子；这个词不作判定。

examples.en: She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
examples.cn: 宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。

examples.en: The board gave its countenance to the merger.
examples.cn: 董事会支持这项合并。

examples.en: The school would not countenance cheating.
examples.cn: 学校不会容许作弊。

dict_mnemonic.text: count（一起）+ ten（握住）+ ance：把自我端住的那张脸，就是「面容」，端得住就是「镇定」。

root: 拉丁语 continentia（自我控制），源自 continere：com-（一起）+ tenere（握住）

sensesIntro.en: Countenance always involves a face holding something; the senses differ in whether it holds a person, a feeling, composure, approval or tolerance.
sensesIntro.cn: countenance 始终涉及一张「端住某物」的脸；各义项的差别在于它端住的是一个人、一种情绪、镇定、认可还是容忍。

core.en: THE FACE AS A CONTAINER
core.cn: 作为容器的脸

branches.en: The face, its expression and its bearing.
branches.cn: 脸、它的表情与仪态。

branches.en: Calmness that keeps the container closed.
branches.cn: 让容器保持关闭的镇定。

branches.en: Support that lends respectability.
branches.cn: 赋予体面地位的支持。

branches.en: Tolerance that stops short of forbidding.
branches.cn: 未到禁止程度的容许。

branches.en: The pressure test that makes composure visible.
branches.cn: 使镇定变得可见的压力测试。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of state with an English form, and its family is the family of holding.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁状态名词的英语形式，其同族词属于「握住」家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show holding together becoming self-control and then social support.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「保持一体」如何变成自我控制，再变成社会支持。

items.example: Endurance is the state of enduring.

definition_zh: 狩猎采集者；以狩猎与采集野生食物为生的人或社会
definition_en: a person who lives by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants
core_image: 一个人清晨握着削尖的木矛、背着编好的草袋，在河岸与林地之间来回察看踪迹与果实
scene: 河岸的泥地上留着鹿蹄印， A hunter-gatherer reads the bank for roots and tracks alike.
sceneCN: 这里 hunter-gatherer 指「以狩猎和采集野生食物为生的人」（第 1 个义项：个体狩猎采集者）；句意为一位狩猎采集者同时察看岸边的根茎与兽迹。图中可辨识物件：木矛、草袋、蹄印、挖根的木棍。

senses.title: A person living by hunting and gathering
senses.definition: an individual whose food comes from hunting animals and collecting wild plants
senses.definitionCN: 食物来自猎取动物与采集野生植物的人
senses.example: A hunter-gatherer moves camp when the fruit stand is stripped.
senses.exampleCN: 果实被摘光后，狩猎采集者就搬营。
senses.why: the compound names the two food-getting activities directly, so the person is defined by the work rather than by ancestry or place.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词直接点出两种获取食物的活动，因此这个人是由劳作而非血统或地点来定义的。

senses.title: A society organised around wild food
senses.titleCN: 围绕野生食物组织起来的社会
senses.definition: a small mobile society whose economy rests on wild resources rather than farming
senses.definitionCN: 经济依赖野生资源而非农耕的小型流动社会
senses.example: The hunter-gatherer society kept no stored surplus beyond a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个狩猎采集社会除几天的份量外不留储备。
senses.why: anthropology uses the singular compound as a category label, so one word can stand for a whole social formation.
senses.whyCN: 人类学把这个单数复合词当作分类标签，因此一个词可以代表一整套社会形态。

senses.title: An archaeological category
senses.definition: a classification for sites and tool kits interpreted as products of wild-food economies
senses.definitionCN: 把遗址与工具组合解释为野生食物经济产物的分类
senses.example: The cave was assigned to a late hunter-gatherer phase.
senses.exampleCN: 这处洞穴被归入狩猎采集的晚期阶段。
senses.why: archaeologists classify what they cannot observe, so the term becomes a label attached to material assemblages.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家给无法直接观察的东西分类，因此这个词成了贴在器物组合上的标签。

senses.title: Attributive use before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe a practice or economy, as in hunter-gatherer diet
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前描述某种做法或经济，如狩猎采集饮食
senses.example: The hunter-gatherer diet included nuts, tubers and small game.
senses.exampleCN: 狩猎采集饮食包括坚果、块根与小猎物。
senses.why: English compounds often work as modifiers without any change of form, so the whole compound sits in front of the noun it qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 英语复合词常不加变化就作修饰语，因此整个复合词直接放在被修饰名词之前。

senses.title: A contemporary group using wild food
senses.titleCN: 当代仍以野生食物为生的群体
senses.definition: a present-day community that still draws much of its food from wild sources
senses.definitionCN: 今天仍以相当部分食物取自野生来源的社群
senses.example: The hunter-gatherer community also sells honey at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个狩猎采集社群也在市场上卖蜂蜜。
senses.why: the term is not only historical: some communities combine wild food with wage work and trade.
senses.whyCN: 这个词并非只属历史：有些社群把野生食物与打工贸易结合起来。

senses.title: A label in development writing
senses.definition: a category used by administrators and aid agencies when describing remote communities
senses.definitionCN: 行政与援助机构描述偏远社群时使用的类别
senses.example: The report's hunter-gatherer label hid the village's wage work.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里「狩猎采集者」的标签掩盖了该村的打工收入。
senses.why: outside agencies need categories, and a category can flatten a mixed livelihood into a single word.
senses.whyCN: 外部机构需要分类，而分类会把混合生计压成一个词。

senses.title: A role in an ecosystem
senses.definition: the combined niche of a predator and a plant collector within one food web
senses.definitionCN: 同一食物网中捕食者与植物采集者合起来占的生态位
senses.example: The hunter-gatherer niche here is shared with bears and crows.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的狩猎采集生态位与熊和乌鸦共享。
senses.why: ecology borrows the human term for animals that both hunt and collect, preserving the two halves of the compound.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个人类学术语来指既捕猎又采集的动物，保留了复合词的两半。

senses.title: An opportunistic searcher
senses.definition: figuratively, someone who takes whatever is available rather than producing systematically
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指见什么取什么、不系统生产的人
senses.example: As a hunter-gatherer of ideas, he read whatever lay open on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 作为思想的狩猎采集者，他桌上摊着什么就读什么。
senses.why: the compound supplies a ready image of scattered, opportunistic acquisition, which fits intellectual habits too.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词提供了「零散、见机获取」的现成意象，也适用于思想习惯。

intro.en: Hunter-gatherer is an English compound of two native words, each built with the agent suffix -er. There is no Latin root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hunter-gatherer 是由两个英语本族词构成的复合词，各自由表施事的 -er 构成，没有拉丁词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Huntian meant 'to chase game'. Its deeper origin is not established; it has no secure cognates outside English.
items.cn: huntian 意为「追逐猎物」。其更深来源未得到证明；在英语之外没有可靠的同源词。

items.en: Gaderian meant 'to bring together, collect', and is related to the English word together.
items.cn: gaderian 意为「聚拢、收集」，与英语 together 同源。

items.en: Hunt and gather each took the agent suffix -er, giving hunter and gatherer as separate occupations.
items.cn: hunt 与 gather 各自加施事后缀 -er，形成 hunter 与 gatherer 两种分开的行当。

items.en: The two words were joined in the twentieth century, when anthropology wanted one category that did not privilege hunting over collecting.
items.cn: 这两个词在 20 世纪被连在一起，当时人类学需要一个不把狩猎凌驾于采集之上的类别。

items.en: Some researchers now prefer forager, arguing that the compound overstates the role of hunting; source uncertain exactly when the compound first appeared in print.
items.cn: 一些研究者现在更爱用 forager，认为这个复合词夸大了狩猎的比重；该复合词最早见于印刷品的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group is the two halves of the compound and their close forms; the second names other ways of getting food.
note.cn: 第一组是复合词的两半及其近形；第二组是其他获取食物的方式。

entries.definition: A person who hunts; it covers only the animal half of the compound and says nothing about plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指打猎的人；只覆盖复合词中动物那一半，不涉及植物。

entries.definition: A person who collects wild plants or other scattered resources; it leaves hunting out.
entries.definitionCN: 指采集野生植物或其他零散资源的人；不含狩猎。

entries.definition: The activity of chasing and killing game; a noun of action, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 追逐并猎杀猎物的活动；是动作名词，不指人。

entries.definition: The act of collecting things, or a social meeting; only the first sense belongs to this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指收集的动作，也指聚会；只有第一义属于这个复合词。

entries.definition: A person who searches for wild food; many anthropologists prefer it because it does not rank hunting above collecting.
entries.definitionCN: 搜寻野生食物的人；许多人类学者偏爱这个词，因为它不把狩猎排在采集之上。

entries.definition: A person who lives by tending domesticated herds; the animals are owned rather than hunted.
entries.definitionCN: 靠照管家养畜群生活的人；牲畜是拥有的，而非猎取的。

entries.definition: A person who grows crops or keeps stock on managed land; the food is produced rather than found.
entries.definitionCN: 在经营土地上种作物或养牲畜的人；食物是生产出来的，不是找到的。

entries.definition: A person who catches fish; a third subsistence route often grouped with hunting and gathering in classifications.
entries.definitionCN: 捕鱼的人；在分类中常与狩猎采集并列为第三条生计路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Old English verbs, two real agent endings and the phrases the compound keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的古英语动词、两个真实的施事后缀，以及这个复合词常用的搭配。

normal.en: hunt + gather + -er + -er = the person who does both, hyphenated into one word.
normal.cn: hunt + gather + -er + -er = 两样都做的人，用连字符并成一个词。

normal.en: Gather is related to together, so the gatherer is the one who brings scattered things in.
normal.cn: gather 与 together 同源，因此 gatherer 就是把零散东西收拢起来的人。

normal.en: The usual frames are society, band, lifestyle and diet.
normal.cn: 常见框架是 society、band、lifestyle、diet。

normal.en: The plural is simply hunter-gatherers; the compound stays unhyphenated in modern style guides but is often hyphenated for clarity.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 -s；现代体例指南多不加连字符，但为清晰常保留连字符。

normal.en: The word contains no Latin, so its affix story is all English.
normal.cn: 这个词不含拉丁成分，因此它的构词故事全是英语的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a spear and a fibre bag at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手同时握着木矛与纤维袋。

abstract.en: Picture two footprints, one from chasing and one from stooping to pick.
abstract.cn: 想象两个脚印，一个来自追赶，一个来自弯腰采摘。

abstract.en: Picture a larder that is the whole landscape, opened a little each day.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片风景就是食物柜，每天只打开一点点。

examples.en: The band of hunter-gatherers moved camp when the waterhole dried.
examples.cn: 水洼干涸后，这群狩猎采集者搬了营。

examples.en: The museum compares hunter-gatherer tool kits from three continents.
examples.cn: 博物馆比较来自三个大陆的狩猎采集工具组合。

examples.en: Modern hunter-gatherer communities also trade with settled neighbours.
examples.cn: 当代狩猎采集社群也与定居邻人贸易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喊它该着」——喊它（猎物）该着跑，一边喊一边捡，猎与采两手都干，就是狩猎采集者。

root: hunter 出自古英语 huntian「追逐猎物」，加施事后缀 -er；gatherer 出自古英语 gaderian「聚拢、收集」，与 together 同源，也加 -er。两者在 20 世纪合成人类学术语，全词无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the individual, widen to the society, the archaeological label and the attributive use, then move to living communities, policy labels, an ecological niche and a metaphorical searcher.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从个人开始，扩到社会、考古标签与定语用法，再到当代社群、政策标签、生态位与比喻性的搜寻者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spear in one hand and a gathering bag on the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一手握矛，背上背一只采集袋。

branches.en: PERSON AND PEOPLE: one worker and a whole society are the same economy at two scales.
branches.cn: 个人与人群：一个劳作者与整个社会，是同一经济在两个尺度上的样子。

branches.en: THE DIG: archaeology files the term onto sites and tools it cannot watch being used.
branches.cn: 发掘：考古学把这个词归档到那些无法现场观察其使用的遗址与工具上。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND PRESENT DAY: the compound modifies diets and also names communities still living this way.
branches.cn: 做法与当下：这个复合词既修饰饮食，也指仍这样生活的社群。

branches.en: THE LABEL: outside agencies use the word as a box, which can hide mixed livelihoods.
branches.cn: 标签：外部机构把这个词当格子用，从而可能掩盖混合生计。

branches.en: NICHE AND METAPHOR: animals that both hunt and collect share the niche, and an opportunistic reader shares the image.
branches.cn: 生态位与比喻：既猎又采的动物共享这一生态位，见机而读的人也共享这一意象。

intro.en: Hunter-gatherer is made of two native English verbs, two agent endings and a hyphen, with no Latin layer at all.
intro.cn: hunter-gatherer 由两个英语本族动词、两个施事后缀与一个连字符构成，完全没有拉丁层。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative exists for either half; medieval Latin had to borrow Germanic words for fodder, and it never supplied a word for hunting of this kind.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁亲戚；中世纪拉丁语反而要借日耳曼词来表示饲料，也从未提供这类狩猎的词。

items.example: The verb survives unchanged in modern English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在现代英语中原样保留。

items.example: The suffix makes hunter and gatherer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 hunter 与 gatherer。

items.example: The hunter followed the herd for two days.
The gatherer filled a bag with acorns.

items.meaning: one who lives by both activities
items.example: The term was coined for a whole economy.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语是为整套经济而造的。

items.meaningCN: 以野生食物为生的人们
items.exampleCN: 狩猎采集者随季节迁移。

items.meaning: a three-part term used where fishing matters
items.meaningCN: 在渔业重要处使用的三段式术语
items.example: Coastal groups are often called hunter-fisher-gatherers.
items.exampleCN: 沿海群体常被称作狩猎捕鱼采集者。

derivatives.meaningCN: 指整个群体的复数形式

derivatives.meaning: the way of life of such societies

definition_zh: 下意识的；潜意识的；半清醒的；隐约的；潜意识（名词）
definition_en: below the level of ordinary awareness, or the part of the mind that works without being noticed
core_image: 海面上风平浪静，海面下却有一股看不见的洋流，一直在推着船走
scene: 他走进旧教室，没看座位表就径直坐到了自己当年的位置，坐下后才想起这件事。 A subconscious pull toward the old seat made him sit down before he noticed.
sceneCN: 这里 subconscious 指「并未自觉、却仍在推动行为的心理力量」（第 1 个义项：未自觉而影响行为）；句意是一股下意识的牵引让他在察觉之前就坐下了。图中可辨识物件：旧课桌、偏移的路线、水面下的暗流。

pos.zh: 下意识的；潜意识的；未自觉的；隐约的
潜意识；下意识的心理活动

forms.label: 比较级（多与 more 连用）
最高级（多与 most 连用）

derivatives.zh: 无意识的 / 潜意识（精神分析）
前意识的（可被唤回但当下不在意识中）

senses.title: Working below awareness
senses.definition: guiding behaviour without the person noticing the guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在当事人并未察觉这种引导的情况下左右其行为
senses.example: A subconscious pull toward the old seat made him sit down before he noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 一股下意识的牵引让他在察觉之前就坐到了老位置上。
senses.why: the word simply places consciousness under something, so what happens there is real but unlighted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是把意识放到某层之下，因此那一层发生的事真实存在，却没有被照亮。

senses.title: Stored but not recalled
senses.titleCN: 存着却未被唤起的记忆
senses.definition: a memory or impression kept in the mind that shapes reactions without being brought to mind
senses.definitionCN: 留在心里、能影响反应却不会被主动想起的记忆或印象
senses.example: A subconscious memory of the song kept him humming it.
senses.exampleCN: 对那首歌的潜意识记忆让他一直哼着它。
senses.why: storage is the oldest idea attached to this word: the file is there, but nobody has opened it.
senses.whyCN: 「储存」是这个词最古老的附着观念：档案在那里，只是没人打开。

senses.title: Only half awake
senses.definition: in a drowsy or drugged state where some response is possible but full awareness is not
senses.definitionCN: 在昏沉或药效之中，能作出部分反应，却没有完整觉察
senses.example: The patient was subconscious enough to mumble but not to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 病人半醒半睡，能含糊出声，却不能作答。
senses.why: this sense stays close to the literal image of a level below the surface: partly above, partly below.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项贴近字面意象：水面之下的那一层，一半在上，一半在下。

senses.title: The hidden part of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心智中隐藏的那一部分
senses.definition: the region of mental life thought to operate outside ordinary attention
senses.definitionCN: 被认为在日常注意之外运作的那块心理领域
senses.example: Early psychologists mapped a conscious, a subconscious and an unconscious layer.
senses.exampleCN: 早期心理学家划分出意识、潜意识与无意识三层。
senses.why: as a noun the word turns the adjective into a place, which is how maps of the mind are drawn.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词把形容词变成一个地点，心智地图正是这样画出来的。

senses.title: Its contents and workings
senses.definition: the wishes, images and habits that live in that hidden region
senses.definitionCN: 居住在那个隐藏区域里的愿望、意象与习惯
senses.example: Dreams were read as messages from the subconscious.
senses.exampleCN: 梦被读作潜意识传来的讯息。
senses.why: a place needs furniture, so the same noun comes to mean everything stored in it as well.
senses.whyCN: 地点需要家具，于是同一个名词也指储存在其中的全部东西。

senses.title: An unspoken resistance
senses.definition: a reluctance or aversion that shows in behaviour before it can be explained
senses.definitionCN: 先表现在行为上、却还说不清理由的抗拒或反感
senses.example: He felt a subconscious resistance whenever the topic of money came up.
senses.exampleCN: 一谈到钱，他心里就生出一股下意识的抗拒。
senses.why: when the hidden layer pushes against something, the push arrives as a feeling before it arrives as a reason.
senses.whyCN: 当隐藏的那层对某物施力时，这股力先以感觉抵达，再以理由抵达。

senses.title: The undercurrent in art
senses.definition: an emotional current beneath the surface of a text, performance or design
senses.definitionCN: 文本、表演或设计表面之下的一股情绪暗流
senses.example: Critics heard a subconscious grief under the cheerful melody.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家听出欢快旋律之下有一种潜意识的哀伤。
senses.why: the term is borrowed for works of art because a work also has a surface and something moving beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被借去谈艺术作品，因为作品同样有表面，也有在表面之下流动的东西。

senses.title: A layer between two others
senses.titleCN: 夹在另两层之间的那一层
senses.definition: in some psychological models, the tier that sits below the conscious and above the unconscious
senses.definitionCN: 在某些心理学模型里，位于意识之下、无意识之上的那一层
senses.example: The model treats the subconscious as a corridor rather than a room.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把潜意识当作一条走廊，而不是一个房间。
senses.why: the prefix means under, not fully away, so the word fits a middle position whenever a three-part map is used.
senses.whyCN: 前缀的意思是「在下」，而不是「完全离开」，因此在三分地图里它正好占中间位置。

intro.en: Subconscious is a modern learned compound of Latin origin: the prefix sub- 'under' placed before conscious. It was coined in the nineteenth century, when psychology needed a term for mental activity that is real but unlighted. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subconscious 是近代按拉丁语素造出的学术复合词：把表「在下」的前缀放在 conscious 之前。19 世纪造出，当时心理学需要一个名称，指真实存在却未被照亮的心理活动。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub meant 'under, below, beneath'. English freely attaches it to adjectives and nouns to place something at a lower level, as in submarine or subtitle.
items.cn: sub 意为「在下、低于、底下」。英语自由地把它加在形容词与名词前，把某物放到较低层级，如潜水艇、副标题。

items.en: The second element is the Latin-derived adjective for being aware, itself built on a prefix meaning 'together' and a verb meaning 'to know'.
items.cn: 第二个成分是那个来自拉丁、表示「觉察」的形容词，它本身由表「共同」的前缀和表「知道」的动词构成。

items.en: The compound appears in nineteenth-century psychological writing, alongside the older negative form, to name mental work that goes on under the threshold of attention.
items.cn: 这个词组出现在 19 世纪心理学著述中，与更早的否定形式并用，用来命名在注意阈限之下进行的心理活动。

items.en: Twentieth-century popular psychology and advertising carried the word out of the clinic, so that it now also describes ordinary unthinking habits.
items.cn: 20 世纪的通俗心理学与广告把它带出诊所，于是它如今也用来描述日常中不过脑的习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first use of the compound is not fixed, and whether it was modelled on a German term of the same shape is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个词组最早的确切用例未定；它是否仿照同形的德语术语造出，属于假说而非已证实的事实。

note.en: Group one holds the prefixed neighbours that are constantly mixed up; group two holds words for what happens outside attention.
note.cn: 第一组是带前缀、极易混用的邻近词；第二组是表示「注意之外所发生之事」的词。

entries.definition: The negative prefix says 'not aware', so it covers fainting and complete unawareness; subconscious says 'under awareness', which still allows a faint rim of knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 否定前缀表示「不觉察」，因此涵盖昏厥与完全不知；subconscious 表示「在觉察之下」，仍允许有一圈微弱的知。

entries.definition: A term for material that is not in mind at the moment but can be recalled at once, sitting just outside rather than underneath.
entries.definitionCN: 指当下不在心中、却能立刻唤回的材料，位置是在外面而非下面。

entries.definition: The state of being unaware, often used for coma; it is a condition, not a layer of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 不觉察的状态，常用于昏迷；是一种状况，而非心智的一层。

entries.definition: The abstract noun of this adjective; it stresses the state, while subconscious usually stresses the place or the influence.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词的抽象名词形式；侧重状态，而 subconscious 通常侧重位置或影响。

entries.definition: Built into the species rather than stored in one mind; an instinctive reaction needs no personal history behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 是物种天生具备的，而非存在某一颗心里；本能反应不需要个人经历作背景。

entries.definition: Describes acts outside conscious control, such as a blink; it names the lack of will rather than the hidden cause.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不受意识控制的行为，如眨眼；它指出的是「无意志」，而非隐藏的起因。

entries.definition: Said of knowledge or bias that is present but not spelled out; it can be fully conscious, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在却未被明说的知识或偏见；它可以是完全自觉的，因此不是同义词。

entries.definition: Names what lies beneath and explains what is seen, without implying anything about awareness at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于其下、能解释可见现象的东西，完全不涉及觉察与否。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'under': the subconscious is literally the conscious layer placed lower.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在下」：潜意识字面上就是把意识那层放到下面。

normal.en: The family runs subconscious, subconsciously, subconsciousness, conscious, unconscious, preconscious.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 subconscious、subconsciously、subconsciousness、conscious、unconscious、preconscious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: the subconscious mind, subconscious bias, at a subconscious level.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：潜意识、不自觉的偏见、在潜意识层面。

normal.en: The three-layer model conscious, subconscious, unconscious is the usual diagram this word sits in.
normal.cn: 意识、潜意识、无意识这三层模型，正是这个词通常所在的那张图。

normal.en: Advertising and popular psychology are the two places the word spread fastest.
normal.cn: 广告与通俗心理学是这个词扩散最快的两个地方。

abstract.en: Picture a current below a calm surface that moves the boat while the sailor sees only glass.
abstract.cn: 想象平静水面下的一股洋流，水手只看见镜面，船却被推着走。

abstract.en: Picture a file left in a drawer that still changes how the room is arranged.
abstract.cn: 想象一份留在抽屉里的档案，仍在改变房间的摆法。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper just below the range of hearing that still makes you turn your head.
abstract.cn: 想象一声刚好在听觉范围之下的低语，仍让你转过头。

examples.en: Subconscious habits often survive even when the reason behind them is gone.
examples.cn: 下意识的习惯常常在背后的理由消失之后仍然保留。

examples.en: She chose the same colour again, on a subconscious level.
examples.cn: 她在潜意识层面又一次选了同一个颜色。

examples.en: The advertisement works on the subconscious rather than on argument.
examples.cn: 这则广告作用于潜意识，而非诉诸论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub（在下）+ conscious（有意识）——意识下面那一层 → 下意识的、潜意识

root: 拉丁语素复合：表「在下」的前缀 sub 加 conscious（源自拉丁 conscius「与……同知」）；19 世纪心理学造词，用来指注意阈限之下仍在运作的心理活动。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a current runs under the surface, and that current is then named as a place, filled with contents, felt as resistance, borrowed for art and finally placed between two other layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：一股水流在表面之下运行，随后这股水流被命名成一个地方、被填进内容、被感觉为抗拒、被借去谈艺术，最后被放到另外两层之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current under a calm surface, moving the boat while the sailor sees only still water.
core.cn: 核心意象：平静表面下的一股水流，水手只看见静止的水，船却在移动。

branches.en: THE CURRENT AND THE WATERLINE: one sense is the pull itself, the other is a person whose awareness sits exactly at the surface.
branches.cn: 水流与水面线：一个义项是牵引本身，另一个是觉察恰好停在水面上的那种人。

branches.en: THE UNOPENED FILE: what is kept below is not gone, only unread, and it still changes reactions.
branches.cn: 未打开的档案：存在下面的东西并未消失，只是没被读，仍在改变反应。

branches.en: A PLACE AND ITS ADDRESS: the noun turns the layer into a location, and the model gives that location a middle floor.
branches.cn: 地点与它的门牌：名词把这一层变成一个位置，而模型又给这个位置安排了一个中间楼层。

branches.en: THE FURNITURE OF THAT PLACE: wishes, images and dreams are what the hidden room is said to hold.
branches.cn: 那个地点的家具：愿望、意象与梦，就是据说藏在暗室里的东西。

branches.en: THE CURRENT FELT OUTSIDE: it reaches us as resistance in the body, or as an undercurrent in a work of art.
branches.cn: 水流在外被感知：它抵达我们时，要么是身体里的抗拒，要么是艺术品底下的暗流。

intro.en: The word is built from two Latin elements, one a prefix of position and one an adjective of awareness, so both halves are transparent.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分搭成：一个是表位置的前缀，一个是表觉察的形容词，两半都很透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- 'under' is the same prefix seen in submarine and subordinate; the base adjective goes back to a verb meaning 'to know'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀表示「在下」，与潜水艇、下属两词中的前缀相同；词基形容词则上溯到一个意为「知道」的动词。

items.example: The prefix places the whole word at a lower level.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把整个词放到较低层级。

items.example: The base supplies the idea of awareness.
A subconscious pull made him sit down.
items.exampleCN: 一股下意识的牵引让他坐了下来。
他不自觉地模仿了她的动作。

items.meaning: the state of being below awareness
items.example: The term names a state rather than a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语命名的是状态，而不是地点。

items.example: She was unconscious for a minute.

items.meaning: just outside awareness but easily recalled
items.meaningCN: 在觉察之外却易被唤回的
items.example: A preconscious memory surfaced at once.
items.exampleCN: 一段前意识的记忆立刻浮现。

items.meaning: a vessel that travels under the sea
items.example: The same prefix shows its positional force here.
items.exampleCN: 同一个前缀在这里显出它的位置义。

definition_zh: 区分；辨别；歧视；区别对待
definition_en: to perceive a difference between things, or to treat people unequally because of their group
core_image: 用筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开
scene: 招聘会上，面试官翻着一份简历，年龄栏被红笔圈起。 At the job fair the interviewer discriminated against an applicant because of her age.
sceneCN: 这里 discriminate 是「歧视」（第 4 个义项：因群体身份而不公平对待）；句意：招聘会上，面试官因为年龄而歧视一位应聘者。

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 区分开

senses.title: Perceive a difference
senses.definition: to notice that two things are different
senses.definitionCN: 注意到两件事物不同
senses.example: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。
senses.why: Latin discriminare means 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'distinction'. The first English sense, 1620s, is the mental act of marking that division.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 discriminare 意为“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”。英语最早义（17 世纪 20 年代）就是在心里标记这条分界。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.titleCN: 把一物与另一物区分开
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between two specific things
senses.definitionCN: 认出两个具体事物之间的差异
senses.example: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。
senses.why: The verb takes two objects because the line is drawn between them. discrimen is the interval or mark between two things, so discrimination is always relational.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词带两个宾语，因为线是在两者之间画的。discrimen 就是两物之间的间隔或标记，所以“区分”总是关系性的。

senses.title: Show fine judgment or taste
senses.definition: to show the ability to make careful distinctions, especially in quality
senses.definitionCN: 表现出仔细辨别、尤指辨别品质的能力
senses.example: She has a discriminating palate for wine.
senses.exampleCN: 她对葡萄酒有敏锐的鉴别力。
senses.why: The adjective discriminating (1792) is the positive side of the same skill. A person who can sift fine differences is said to have taste, not prejudice.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 discriminating（1792）是同一能力的正面面。能筛出细微差异的人被说成品味好，而不是有偏见。

senses.title: Treat people unequally
senses.definition: to treat people differently and unfairly because of their group
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体而不公平地对待人
senses.example: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
senses.exampleCN: 因年龄歧视是违法的。
senses.why: The adverse sense, 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons', is first recorded in 1866 in American English. The neutral line-drawing turns into a hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于 1866 年的美国英语。中性的画线变成了等级。

senses.title: Discriminate against someone
senses.definition: to deny someone opportunities or fair treatment because of who they are
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的身份而剥夺机会或公平待遇
senses.example: The firm was accused of discriminating against women.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被指控歧视女性。
senses.why: The fixed pattern discriminate against makes the target explicit. The verb now names an action with a victim, not merely a perception.
senses.whyCN: 固定搭配 discriminate against 明确点出受害者。这个动词现在指带有受害者的行为，而不只是感知。

senses.title: Separate signals from noise
senses.definition: in electronics, to select wanted signals and reject unwanted ones
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中选出所需信号、排除干扰
senses.example: The circuit discriminates noise from signal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个电路能鉴别噪声与信号。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the original 'sift' image almost literally: a circuit separates one kind of input from another and passes only the wanted kind.
senses.whyCN: 工程学几乎字面保留了“筛”的意象：电路把一类输入与另一类分开，只放行所需的一类。

senses.title: Apply a discriminatory rule
senses.definition: to operate a rule or practice that disadvantages a protected group
senses.definitionCN: 执行使受保护群体处于不利地位的规则或做法
senses.example: Landlords may not discriminate against tenants with children.
senses.exampleCN: 房东不得歧视带孩子的租户。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the verb into a name for a prohibited practice. The distinction is no longer neutral; the law defines which lines may not be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个动词变成对禁止行为的称呼。区分不再中性；法律界定哪些线不得画。

senses.title: Distinct, marked off (archaic adjective)
senses.titleCN: 独特的；被区分开的（古形容词）
senses.definition: in 17c. use, an adjective meaning 'distinct'
senses.definitionCN: 在 17 世纪用法中作形容词，意为“独特的”
senses.example: In 17c. texts a discriminate difference meant a clearly marked one.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪文本中，a discriminate difference 指被清楚标出的差异。
senses.why: The adjective sense, recorded 1620s, meant 'distinct'; the later sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798. It survives mainly inside discriminating and indiscriminate.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“独特的”；后来“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。它主要残留在 discriminating 与 indiscriminate 中。

intro.en: Discriminate began as a neutral act of separating, then acquired one of the strongest social meanings in English. The root cernere 'to sift' explains both the neutral and the contested senses.
intro.cn: discriminate 起初是中性的“分开”动作，后来获得英语中最强烈的社会含义之一。词根 cernere“筛”解释了它的中性义与争议义。

items.en: The verb means 'distinguish from something else or from each other, observe or mark the differences'.
items.cn: 动词义为“把某物与别物区分开，或观察并标记差异”。

items.en: From discriminatus, past participle of discriminare 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'interval, distinction'.
items.cn: 来自 discriminatus，即 discriminare“分开、分离”的过去分词，源头是 discrimen“间隔、区别”。

items.en: discrimen derives from discernere 'to separate, sift, distinguish', from dis- 'off, away' + cernere 'sift' (PIE *krei- 'to sieve').
items.cn: discrimen 来自 discernere“分开、筛、辨别”，由 dis-“离开”+ cernere“筛”（原始印欧语 *krei-“筛”）。

items.en: An adjective sense 'distinct' is recorded; the sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798.
items.cn: 形容词义“独特的”被记录；“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。

items.en: discriminating 'possessing discernment' appears, the positive side of the same skill.
items.cn: discriminating“有辨别力的”出现，是同一能力的正面面。

items.en: The adverse sense 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons' is first recorded in American English.
items.cn: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于美国英语。

note.en: The first group is about forms in the same family; the second is about verbs that also tell things apart.
note.cn: 第一组看同一词族的形态，第二组看同样把事物区分开的动词。

entries.definition: showing careful judgment and good taste; the positive sense of the skill.
entries.definitionCN: 有鉴别力的；品味好的（该能力的正面义）。

entries.definition: unfairly treating a group; the negative institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 歧视性的；不公平对待群体的（负面的制度义）。

entries.definition: done without choosing carefully; random or widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区分的；随意的（in- 表否定）。

entries.definition: to see or show a difference, often with careful attention. It is neutral and broad.
entries.definitionCN: 看出或表明差异，常含仔细留意。它中性而宽泛。

entries.definition: to make or recognize a difference, especially in a technical or systematic way.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同或认出差异，尤指技术性、系统性地。

entries.definition: to perceive something with difficulty or subtlety. It stresses the effort of seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 费力或细微地察觉某物。它强调“看见”的努力。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the root cernere 'sift', the 1866 social sense, the positive discriminating, and the legal pattern discriminate against.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：词根 cernere“筛”、1866 年的社会义、正面的 discriminating，以及法律搭配 discriminate against。

normal.en: The root cernere means 'to sift'. To discriminate is to pass things through a sieve and keep the wanted grains.
normal.cn: 词根 cernere 意为“筛”。discriminate 就是把东西过筛，留下想要的颗粒。

normal.en: discrimen is the interval between two things; a distinction exists only where two items meet.
normal.cn: discrimen 是两物之间的间隔；只有两物相遇之处才有区分。

normal.en: discriminating taste is the same sieve used well: fine differences are kept, coarse ones rejected.
normal.cn: discriminating taste 就是使用得当的同一张筛子：留下细微差异，筛掉粗糙之处。

normal.en: In 1866 American English the neutral sieve became a hierarchy: some people were sorted out and denied fair treatment.
normal.cn: 1866 年美国英语中，中性的筛子变成了等级：一些人被筛出去，失去公平待遇。

normal.en: The legal pattern discriminate against names a victim, which is why it is the strongest use of the word.
normal.cn: 法律搭配 discriminate against 点明受害者，因此是这个词语气最强的用法。

abstract.en: Discrimination is selection: every sieve includes and excludes at once. The ethics lie in who chose the mesh.
abstract.cn: 区分就是选择：每张筛子都同时容纳与排除。伦理在于是谁选了筛孔。

abstract.en: The word holds both discernment and prejudice because both are acts of sorting; only the purpose separates them.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时容纳“鉴别力”与“偏见”，因为两者都是分拣动作；区分它们的是目的。

abstract.en: A just distinction marks differences without using them to deny a share; an unjust one turns a difference into a rank.
abstract.cn: 公正的区分标出差异却不借此剥夺份额；不公正的区分把差异变成等级。

examples.en: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
examples.cn: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。

examples.en: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
examples.cn: 因年龄歧视是违法的。

examples.en: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
examples.cn: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地是亏米”——地里的米亏了，要筛一筛分开好坏 → discriminate 区分、歧视

root: 拉丁语 discriminare“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”，再上为 discernere“筛、辨别”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of discriminate, all built on one act: sifting. Sifting can be neutral (telling kinds apart), skilled (good taste), technical (separating signal from noise), or unjust (denying a group fair treatment).
sensesIntro.cn: discriminate 的八个义项都建立在一个动作上：筛。筛可以是中性的（分出种类）、有技巧的（好品味）、技术的（分离信号与噪声），或是不义的（剥夺某群体的公平待遇）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve separating grains of different sizes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开。

branches.en: SEPARATE: the neutral core, drawing a line between two kinds and telling them apart.
branches.cn: 分开：中性核心，在两类之间画线并把它们辨开。

branches.en: MARKED OFF: the old adjective describes the thing that has been separated and stands distinct.
branches.cn: 被标出：旧形容词描述已被分开、独自成立之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: the same sieve used with skill produces discriminating taste.
branches.cn: 品质：同一张筛子用得娴熟，就产生有鉴别力的品味。

branches.en: PREJUDICE: the line becomes a hierarchy and denies fair treatment.
branches.cn: 偏见：线变成等级，剥夺公平待遇。

branches.en: SIGNAL: engineering keeps the literal sieve, passing one kind of input only.
branches.cn: 信号：工程学保留字面的筛，只放行一类输入。

intro.en: Discriminate is built on the Latin stem discrimin-. English adds -tion, -tory, -ting, -tive, -able, and the negative prefixes in- and non-.
intro.cn: discriminate 建立在拉丁词干 discrimin- 上。英语加 -tion、-tory、-ting、-tive、-able，以及否定前缀 in-、non-。

latinIntro.en: Latin discriminare, discrimen, and discernere all belong to the 'sift' family. Cernere 'to sift' also underlies discern, secret, and certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discriminare、discrimen、discernere 都属于“筛”的词族。cernere“筛”也是 discern、secret、certain 的深层来源。

items.meaning: the act of distinguishing; also, unfair treatment of a group
items.meaningCN: 区分；歧视（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: showing careful judgment and fine taste
having been distinguished or treated unfairly

definition_zh: 疏散；撤离；排空；排泄
definition_en: to move people away from a dangerous place, or to empty a container, a space, or the body of what is inside it
core_image: 一队人拎着行李走出空荡的楼，门在身后关上，屋里只剩下回声
scene: 洪水漫过街道，救援队挨家敲门，把居民送到高处。 Rescue teams helped evacuate the whole street before the river rose further.
sceneCN: 这里 evacuate 是「疏散人员」（第 1 个义项：把人从危险的地方转移出去）；句意：救援队赶在河水继续上涨前帮助疏散了整条街的人。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「疏散；撤离；排空」
由本词加 -ee（受动作影响的人）构成，义为「被疏散者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「促排泄的；用于排空的」

senses.title: To move people out of danger
senses.definition: to move people away from a place where they are in danger, usually in an organised way
senses.definitionCN: 通常有组织地把人从有危险的地方转移出去
senses.example: Fire officers evacuated the hotel within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 消防人员在十分钟内疏散了旅馆里的人。
senses.why: Latin e- or ex- means out and vacuus means empty: to evacuate is to make a place empty of its people, and the danger is the reason for emptying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 e- 与 ex- 意为「出」，vacuus 意为「空」：evacuate 就是让一个地方在人这方面变空，危险则是把地方腾空的理由。

senses.title: To leave a place
senses.definition: of people, troops, or an organisation, to leave a place that is being given up or is no longer safe
senses.definitionCN: 指人员、部队或机构离开一个被放弃或已不安全的地方
senses.example: The staff evacuated the office when the alarm sounded.
senses.exampleCN: 警报响起时，员工撤离了办公室。
senses.why: Once the place is emptied, the people who leave are the ones doing the emptying, so the subject of the verb shifts from the building to the people.
senses.whyCN: 地方一旦被腾空，离开的人就成了执行腾空的一方，于是动词的主语从建筑物转到了人身上。

senses.title: To empty a container or space
senses.definition: to remove the contents of a container, a vessel, or an enclosed space, leaving it empty
senses.definitionCN: 把容器、管道或封闭空间中的东西取出，使其变空
senses.example: Engineers evacuated the tank before the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在检查前把罐体排空了。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal use of the Latin verb, which simply meant to make something empty, with no danger involved at all.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语动词最古老、最字面的用法，意思只是「使某物变空」，完全不含危险的意思。

senses.title: To discharge waste from the body
senses.definition: to pass waste matter out of the bowels or another part of the body, a medical and formal use
senses.definitionCN: 把废物从肠道或身体其他部位排出，属医学与正式用法
senses.example: The patient had not evacuated the bowels for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 病人已经三天没有排便了。
senses.why: Latin medical writers used evacuare for clearing the body of humours and waste, so the emptying image was applied to the inside of the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁医学作者用 evacuare 表示把体液与废物从体内清出，于是「腾空」的意象被用到了身体内部。

senses.title: To remove air or gas
senses.definition: in technical use, to draw air or gas out of a sealed space so that a vacuum is left
senses.definitionCN: 技术用语，把空气或气体从密闭空间中抽出，留下真空
senses.example: The chamber is evacuated before the samples are sealed in.
senses.exampleCN: 样品密封进去之前，腔体要先抽真空。
senses.why: A sealed space is a container, and its contents happen to be gas, so taking the gas out is emptying it in the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 密闭空间就是一个容器，只是里面装的东西恰好是气体，把气体取出来，正是最字面意义上的「腾空」。

intro.en: Evacuate comes straight from Latin evacuare, built on vacuus, empty, and the prefix e- or ex-, out.
intro.cn: evacuate 直接来自拉丁语 evacuare，由 vacuus「空的」与前缀 e- 或 ex-「出」构成。

items.en: Vacuus means empty or free of occupants, and it also gives vacuum and vacant.
items.cn: vacuus 意为空的、无人占用的，也是 vacuum 与 vacant 的来源。

items.en: The verb vacare means to be empty or to be free of something.
items.cn: 动词 vacare 意为空着、没有被占用。

items.en: Ex plus vacuus formed evacuare, to empty out, with the past participle evacuatus.
items.cn: ex 与 vacuus 构成 evacuare，意为「把……腾空」，过去分词是 evacuatus。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century first for clearing the body and emptying vessels.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，最初用于清空身体与排空器皿。

items.en: Military use added the sense of withdrawing troops from a place, and the civilian sense of moving people out followed.
items.cn: 军事用法增加了「把部队撤出某地」的意思，随后又有了转移平民的用法。

items.en: Modern disaster language made evacuate a household word for moving people out of floods, fires, and storms.
items.cn: 现代灾害语言让 evacuate 成为「把人们撤出洪水、火灾与风暴」的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the vacuus family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of leaving and emptying.
note.cn: 形近组收 vacuus 这一词族；近义组收表示离开与腾空的动词。

entries.definition: the act of moving people out or emptying a space, formed with -ion
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疏散、撤离、排空」，由动词加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: a person who has been moved out of a dangerous place, formed with -ee
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被疏散者」，由动词加 -ee 构成。

entries.definition: a space with nothing in it, from the same Latin word for empty
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「真空、空白」，来自同一个表示「空」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: to pull back troops or people from a place, stressing a deliberate retreat
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤出、撤退」，强调有意的后撤。

entries.definition: to take everything out of a container, with no suggestion of danger
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倒空、腾空」，不含危险的意味。

entries.definition: to leave a place or a person behind for good, with a stronger sense of desertion
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弃置、抛下」，带有更强的遗弃意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin pieces of the word and the phrases the verb really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词的拉丁语构件，以及它真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: E- is out and vacuus is empty: to evacuate is to empty a place out.
normal.cn: e- 是「出」，vacuus 是「空」：evacuate 就是把一个地方腾空。

normal.en: Vacuum, vacant, and vacate share the same empty root.
normal.cn: vacuum、vacant 与 vacate 共用同一个表示「空」的词根。

normal.en: You evacuate a building, but you also evacuate your bowels: both are emptying.
normal.cn: evacuate 可以接 building，也可以接 bowels：两者都是「腾空」。

normal.en: The passive is common: residents were evacuated to safety.
normal.cn: 被动式很常见：居民被转移到安全地带。

normal.en: Compare empty: empty is neutral, while evacuate usually implies a threat or an order.
normal.cn: 对比 empty：empty 是中性的，而 evacuate 通常暗示威胁或命令。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people carrying bags out of a lit doorway, a warden counting them as they pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人拎着包从亮着的门口出来，引导员在门口清点人数。

abstract.en: Picture an empty office with the lights still on and a cup of tea going cold on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空掉的办公室，灯还亮着，桌上的茶正在变凉。

abstract.en: Picture a tank with its valve open, the last of the liquid running out and the metal ringing hollow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只打开阀门的罐子，最后的液体流尽，金属敲起来发出空响。

examples.en: Police evacuated the market after the gas leak was reported.
examples.cn: 接到燃气泄漏的报告后，警方疏散了市场里的人。

examples.en: The whole village was evacuated before the dam broke.
examples.cn: 大坝决口前，整个村子的人都被疏散了。

examples.en: Nurses evacuated the ward quietly, moving patients to the lower floor.
examples.cn: 护士们安静地撤离了病房，把病人转移到楼下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一挖空」——evacuate 读起来像「一挖空」：房间挖空、街道撤空；纯属谐音拆词联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 e- 与 ex-（出）＋ vacuus（空的）→ evacuare（把……腾空，过去分词 evacuatus）→ 英语 evacuate；核心义「使变空」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all empty something out: a dangerous place of its people, a place of its occupants, a container of its contents, the body of its waste, and a sealed chamber of its air.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在把某样东西腾空：危险之地的人、被放弃之地的占用者、容器的内容物、身体的废物，以及密闭腔体里的空气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people leaving a building that stands empty behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人走出身后的空楼。

branches.en: THE ALARM: making a dangerous place empty of people is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 警报线：让危险之地在人这方面变空，是日常义项。

branches.en: THE DEPARTURE: the people who empty the place are seen leaving it.
branches.cn: 离开线：执行腾空的人被看作离开的人。

branches.en: THE VESSEL: emptying a container is the oldest and most literal use.
branches.cn: 容器线：排空容器是最古老、最字面的用法。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE CHAMBER: waste and gas are just contents to be taken out.
branches.cn: 身体与腔体线：废物和气体不过是需要取出的内容物。

branches.en: All three keep one frame: a space is made empty, whether by people leaving or by contents being removed.
branches.cn: 三个义项共用同一个框架：空间被腾空，或靠人离开，或靠内容物被取走。

intro.en: Evacuate joins a Latin prefix of exit to a Latin adjective of emptiness, and English adds the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: evacuate 把表示「出」的拉丁语前缀接到表示「空」的拉丁语形容词上，英语再加上动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus, vacare, and evacuare are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root behind vacuus is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus、vacare 与 evacuare 都有文献记录，只有 vacuus 背后更早的印欧词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks the movement outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的动作。

items.example: Vacuus is the adjective of emptiness.
items.exampleCN: vacuus 是表示「空」的形容词。

items.meaning: to be empty, to be free
items.example: Vacare is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: vacare 是这个形容词背后的动词。

items.example: The prefix and the adjective made this verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与形容词合成了这个动词。

items.example: It forms evacuate from the Latin participle.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁语分词构成 evacuate。

items.meaning: a space with nothing in it
items.example: Vacuum keeps the Latin neuter form.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 保留了拉丁语的中性形式。

items.example: Vacant keeps the same empty root.
items.exampleCN: vacant 保留同一个表示「空」的词根。

items.meaning: the act of emptying or moving people out

latinEntries.example: Vacuus is the source of vacuum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vacuus 是 vacuum 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Vacare gives the verb family its shape.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vacare 给这一动词族定下形态。

latinEntries.example: Evacuare is the direct source of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: evacuare 是这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 胚胎；（事物的）雏形；胚
definition_en: the unborn or newly developing young of an organism, or the earliest form of something
core_image: 一粒种子被切开，里面蜷着一条极小的根与芽，整个未来的植株已经按比例缩小藏在这里
scene: 在植物实验室里，技术员切开一枚种子说： The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
sceneCN: 这里 embryo 指「种子内处于早期发育阶段的胚」（第 3 个义项：植物种子中的胚）；句意是种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。

pos.zh: 胚胎；胚；雏形；（事物的）初期形态

senses.title: The developing young of an animal
senses.definition: the unborn or newly developing young of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 动物未出生或刚发育的幼体
senses.example: The embryo implants in the womb about a week after fertilization.
senses.exampleCN: 受精约一周后，胚胎着床于子宫。
senses.why: Greek embryon named the young one still forming inside, so the noun points at the organism before it has taken shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 embryon 指在里面仍在形成的幼体，因此这个名词指尚未成形时的生物体。

senses.title: A human embryo in its early stage
senses.definition: a human organism in the first weeks after fertilization
senses.definitionCN: 受精后最初数周的人类生物体
senses.example: The human embryo is called a fetus after the eighth week.
senses.exampleCN: 人类胚胎在第八周之后被称为胎儿。
senses.why: Medicine needs a boundary, so embryo marks the early weeks before the fetal stage begins.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一条界线，因此 embryo 标记胎儿阶段开始之前的最初数周。

senses.title: The plant embryo inside a seed
senses.definition: the young plant contained within a seed
senses.definitionCN: 包含在种子内的幼小植株
senses.example: The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
senses.exampleCN: 种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。
senses.why: Plants package the young plant inside a seed, and botany uses the same noun for that dormant form.
senses.whyCN: 植物把幼株包在种子里，植物学用同一个名词指这种休眠形态。

senses.title: The earliest form of something
senses.definition: the beginning or germ of something that will develop further
senses.definitionCN: 将进一步发展之物的开端或雏形
senses.example: The first sketch was the embryo of the finished building.
senses.exampleCN: 第一幅草图是这座建成建筑的前身。
senses.why: Because an embryo contains the whole future in miniature, the noun extends to any early germ of a larger thing.
senses.whyCN: 因为胚胎以缩小的形式包含整个未来，这个名词便延伸到任何较大事物的早期雏形。

senses.title: An embryo in assisted reproduction
senses.definition: an embryo produced and transferred in fertility treatment
senses.definitionCN: 生育治疗中培育并移植的胚胎
senses.example: The clinic transferred one embryo and froze the others.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所移植了一个胚胎，把其余的冷冻起来。
senses.why: Reproductive technology makes the embryo an object handled outside the body, giving the noun a clinical sense.
senses.whyCN: 生殖技术使胚胎成为在体外被操作的对象，使这个名词获得临床义。

senses.title: An embryo as a specimen
senses.definition: a preserved or staged embryo used for study
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究而保存或分期的胚胎
senses.example: The collection holds embryos at every stage of development.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品保存着每个发育阶段的胚胎。
senses.why: In a laboratory the embryo becomes a specimen with a stage number, a thing to be compared rather than a future animal.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，胚胎变成带分期编号的标本，是被比较的对象，而非未来的动物。

senses.title: The embryo contrasted with the larva
senses.definition: the developmental stage before hatching, as distinct from a free-living larva
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之前的发育阶段，与自由生活的幼虫相对
senses.example: The embryo develops inside the egg before the larva emerges.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎在卵内发育，之后幼虫才出来。
senses.why: Zoology separates stages by whether the young is still enclosed, and embryo marks the enclosed phase.
senses.whyCN: 动物学按幼体是否仍被包裹来划分阶段，embryo 标记被包裹的阶段。

senses.title: The germ of a plan or design
senses.titleCN: 计划或设计的最初构想
senses.definition: an early idea from which a plan or work may grow
senses.definitionCN: 计划或作品可能由此生长的最初想法
senses.example: The idea remained an embryo for years before anyone funded it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法多年只是雏形，直到有人资助。
senses.why: The biological image gives the noun a figurative life: a plan can be pregnant with a future it has not yet shown.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象给这个名词以比喻生命：一个计划可以孕育着尚未显露的未来。

intro.en: Embryo comes from Greek embryon, a young one still forming, built from en- in and bryein to swell; Latin and English adopted it as a scientific noun.
intro.cn: embryo 来自希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体」，由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成；拉丁语与英语把它作为科学名词吸收。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one, and also a swelling; the word pictured life growing inside a enclosing body.
items.cn: embryon 意为幼体，也指肿块；这个词描绘生命在有包裹的身体内生长。

items.en: En- meant in and bryein meant to swell or be full; the compound's literal sense is swelling within.
items.cn: en- 意为「在内」，bryein 意为「膨胀、充满」；复合词的字面义是「在里面膨胀」。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as embryo and used it in learned writing for the unborn young.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这一希腊名词吸收为 embryo，在学术写作中指未出生的幼体。

items.en: English embryo appeared in the sixteenth century, first in learned and medical contexts.
items.cn: 英语 embryo 在 16 世纪出现，最初用于学术与医学语境。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun was also used for the early form of a thing, a usage that persists in modern writing.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，这个名词也用于指事物的早期形态，这一用法在现代写作中延续。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of bryein is not established, so any Indo-European base offered is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（bryein 词根存疑、年代为约数）：bryein 的更深来源未得到证明，凡为其给出的印欧语基均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same embryo stock; group two holds stages and near terms in developmental biology.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词族的词；第二组是发育生物学中的阶段与近义术语。

entries.definition: Relating to an embryo or to an early stage; it describes, while embryo names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚胎或早期阶段有关的形容词；它作描述，而 embryo 指对象。

entries.definition: The study of embryos; it names a science, not the organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的学科；它指科学，而非生物体。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective for embryonic tissue, used mainly in pathology and anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的形容词，指胚胎组织，主要用于病理学与解剖学。

entries.definition: The nourishing tissue inside a seed; it surrounds the plant embryo but is not the embryo itself.
entries.definitionCN: 种子内提供营养的组织；它包围植物胚，但本身不是胚。

entries.definition: The unborn young after the embryonic stage; the two nouns mark successive phases.
entries.definitionCN: 胚胎阶段之后未出生的幼体；两个名词标记相继阶段。

entries.definition: An independent young form that hatches and feeds itself, unlike an embryo still enclosed.
entries.definitionCN: 孵化后独立取食的幼体形态，与仍被包裹的胚胎不同。

entries.definition: The structure that holds the plant embryo with its food supply; the embryo is inside the seed.
entries.definitionCN: 包含植物胚与养分供应的结构；胚在种子内部。

entries.definition: The earliest stage from which something may develop; it is the figurative counterpart of embryo.
entries.definitionCN: 某物可能由此发展的最早阶段；是 embryo 的比喻对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: En- in plus bryein swell: life swelling inside a wrapping.
normal.cn: en-「在内」加 bryein「膨胀」：生命在包裹内膨胀。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryonic, embryology, embryologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryonic、embryology、embryologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: human embryo, plant embryo, embryo transfer, embryo sac.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类胚胎、植物胚、胚胎移植、胚囊。

normal.en: The timeline is embryo, then fetus, then birth.
normal.cn: 时间线是胚胎、胎儿、出生。

normal.en: In seeds the embryo waits, tiny but complete in outline.
normal.cn: 在种子里，胚静静等待，微小却轮廓完整。

abstract.en: Picture a seed cut open to reveal a miniature plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被切开，露出一株缩小的植株。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint folded small enough to fit in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图折得小到能放进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a whole tree sleeping inside one hard shell.
abstract.cn: 想象整棵树睡在一枚硬壳里。

examples.en: The embryo divides rapidly in the first days after fertilization.
examples.cn: 受精后的最初几天，胚胎迅速分裂。

examples.en: Botanists distinguish the embryo from the surrounding food tissue.
examples.cn: 植物学家把胚与周围的营养组织区分开。

examples.en: The novel was still an embryo when the war began.
examples.cn: 战争开始时，这部小说还只是雏形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em 在内 + bryo 膨胀」——在里面膨胀生长的幼体 → 胚胎、雏形

root: 希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体；肿块」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」，经拉丁 embryo 进入英语；bryein 更深词根不确定，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one noun from an animal's developing young to a human stage, a seed's plant, a figurative germ, a clinical object, a museum specimen, a zoological phase and the first form of a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个名词从动物发育中的幼体走向人类阶段、种子里的植株、比喻的雏形、临床对象、博物馆标本、动物学阶段，最后走向计划的最初形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed opened to show a tiny plant that already carries the whole future in outline.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒种子被打开，露出一株已以轮廓携带全部未来的小植株。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL YOUNG: animal, human and plant embryos are the same stage in different containers.
branches.cn: 生物学幼体：动物、人类与植物胚是不同容器中的同一阶段。

branches.en: EARLIEST FORM: anything larger begins as an embryo of itself.
branches.cn: 最初形态：任何更大的事物都以自身的胚胎形态开始。

branches.en: OBJECT OF HANDLING: clinics transfer embryos, museums stage them as specimens.
branches.cn: 被操作的对象：诊所移植胚胎，博物馆把它分期为标本。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: the embryo ends where the free-living larva or fetus begins.
branches.cn: 边界：胚胎在自由生活幼虫或胎儿开始处结束。

branches.en: UNREALIZED FUTURE: the noun names something whose future is still folded inside it.
branches.cn: 未实现的未来：这个名词指未来仍折叠在其内部的事物。

intro.en: Embryo is a Greek noun borrowed whole, but its parts can still be read and compared with other scientific words.
intro.cn: embryo 是一个整体借入的希腊名词，但它的部件仍可读出，并与其他科学词比较。

latinIntro.en: Greek en- and bryein build embryon; the same en- appears in endemic and energy, while bryein is rare outside this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 en- 与 bryein 构成 embryon；同一个 en- 见于 endemic 与 energy，而 bryein 在此词族之外很少见。

items.example: The prefix marks something growing inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记在内部生长之物。

items.example: The verb is confined largely to this family in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在英语中基本只限于这个词族。
embryon 以 embryo 进入拉丁语。

items.example: The embryo is enclosed in the seed.

items.exampleCN: 胚胎学家对样本作了分期。

definition_zh: 藏书癖；藏书狂；对书籍的狂热收集
definition_en: an excessive passion for collecting books
core_image: 书堆埋到天花板，收藏者仍伸手再买一本
scene: 薪水发下来不到三天，他又抱回一箱旧书。 His bibliomania left no room for furniture in the flat.
sceneCN: 这里 bibliomania 是「藏书癖」（第 1 个义项：对收书的病态狂热）；句意是藏书癖让他的公寓里连放家具的地方都没有。

derivatives.zh: bibliomania 加 -ac，义为「有藏书癖的人」
bibliomania 加形容词后缀，义为「藏书癖的」
同根词，义为「爱书人」，程度较缓
基础词，义为「狂热；癖好」，bibliomania 由其构成

senses.title: A craze for collecting books
senses.definition: an uncontrollable, excessive passion for acquiring and hoarding books
senses.definitionCN: 对收书、囤书难以自控的过度狂热
senses.example: His bibliomania left no room for furniture in the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 藏书癖让他的公寓里连放家具的地方都没有。
senses.why: Greek mania means madness, so book-love becomes book-madness.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mania 意为疯狂，爱书便升格为「书痴」。

senses.title: Obsession with rare editions
senses.definition: the obsessive pursuit of rare, first, or fine editions regardless of cost
senses.definitionCN: 不计代价追逐珍本、初版与装帧精美之书
senses.example: His bibliomania for first editions emptied three bank accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 他对初版书的痴迷掏空了三个银行账户。
senses.why: The rarer the book, the hotter the mania burns.
senses.whyCN: 书越珍稀，狂热燃烧得越旺。

senses.title: Collecting for possession, not reading
senses.definition: hoarding books as objects to own rather than texts to read
senses.definitionCN: 把书当作占有物囤积，而非当作读物
senses.example: In full bibliomania, he bought books he never opened.
senses.exampleCN: 藏书癖发作时，他买下从不开卷的书。
senses.why: Possession, not use, is the mania's true aim.
senses.whyCN: 狂热的真正目标是占有，而非使用。

senses.title: The collector's disease (humorous)
senses.definition: a humorous way to describe book-buying as an illness
senses.definitionCN: 以「病」自嘲或调侃买书成瘾
senses.example: The doctor diagnosed a mild case of bibliomania.
senses.exampleCN: 医生诊断出轻度藏书癖。
senses.why: Naming the passion a disease makes the joke.
senses.whyCN: 把爱好称为疾病，幽默便在其中。

senses.title: Fever of auction and bidding
senses.definition: the excited bidding that seizes collectors at book auctions
senses.definitionCN: 藏书者在古籍拍卖会上失控竞价的兴奋
senses.example: Bibliomania gripped the room as the folio came up.
senses.exampleCN: 对开本古籍上拍时，全场的藏书狂热被点燃。
senses.why: The crowd's mania rises like a fever with each bid.
senses.whyCN: 每一次举牌，狂热便如热病升高一度。

senses.title: Historical craze for libraries
senses.definition: the great wave of aristocratic book collecting in earlier centuries
senses.definitionCN: 旧时贵族与富商竞建私库藏书的狂潮
senses.example: Eighteenth-century bibliomania built the great private libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 十八世纪的藏书热造就了那些著名私库。
senses.why: Wealth plus print plus prestige fed a collecting frenzy.
senses.whyCN: 财富、印刷与名望共同喂养了收藏狂潮。

senses.title: Craving for fine bindings
senses.definition: the passion for luxurious bindings, fore-edge paintings, and fine prints
senses.definitionCN: 痴迷于奢华装帧、书口彩绘与精印本
senses.example: Her bibliomania favored gold-tooled morocco bindings.
senses.exampleCN: 她的收藏癖偏爱烫金摩洛哥皮装帧。
senses.why: The book's body, not just its soul, becomes the prize.
senses.whyCN: 成为珍品的不仅是书的灵魂，还有书的躯体。

senses.title: Any passionate specialty in books
senses.definition: a narrow, ardent specialization, such as one subject or format
senses.definitionCN: 对某一题材或形态的窄而炽热的专门收藏
senses.example: His bibliomania ran to cookbooks alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书痴之癖只专注于菜谱。
senses.why: Mania narrows to a single burning channel.
senses.whyCN: 狂热收窄为一条炽热的窄渠。

entries.definition: a lover of books, milder than a maniac
entries.definitionCN: 爱书人——同根，程度较缓

entries.definition: a list of books

entries.definition: an uncontrollable craving for alcohol

entries.definition: a persistent disturbing preoccupation

entries.definition: an excessive enthusiasm or madness

entries.definition: a wild burst of intense activity
entries.definitionCN: 狂乱——侧重发作的瞬间

normal.en: A bibliomaniac is the person.

normal.cn: bibliomaniacal 是形容词。

normal.en: A bibliophile loves books more mildly.

abstract.en: See shelves buckle under mountains of unread spines.
abstract.cn: 看书架被成山的未读书脊压弯。

abstract.en: Feel the pulse quicken at a rare title card.
abstract.cn: 感受见到珍本目录卡时加快的脉搏。

abstract.en: Picture a house where doors are made of stacked books.
abstract.cn: 想象书堆成门、无路可走的屋子。

examples.en: Bibliomania gripped the room as the folio came up.
examples.cn: 对开本古籍上拍时，全场的藏书狂热被点燃。

branches.cn: 占有书籍之狂
