definition_zh: 一丝不苟的；极其仔细的；谨小慎微的
definition_en: showing great attention to small details
core_image: 一个人把一叠发票按日期、金额和颜色对齐，又把最上面一张的边角抚平
scene: 她把每份档案的页码都核了两遍，才肯签字。 His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
sceneCN: 这里 meticulous 指一丝不苟（第 1 个义项：对细节极度仔细）；句意为他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。

pos.zh: 一丝不苟的；极其仔细的

senses.title: Care about small details
senses.definition: giving close attention to details others might skip
senses.definitionCN: 对别人可能略过的细节给予密切注意
senses.example: His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
senses.exampleCN: 他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。
senses.why: The word praises the small: it treats the minor as if it mattered, and often it does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词赞美细小之物：它把次要的当作重要的，而它常常确实重要。

senses.title: Meticulous record-keeping
senses.definition: keeping accounts so exact that nothing needs reconstructing
senses.definitionCN: 记账精确到无需事后重建
senses.example: The clerk kept meticulous records of every delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 这位职员对每次交付都做了精细记录。
senses.why: A record is useful only if it can be trusted without being checked again.
senses.whyCN: 记录只有在无需复查就能被信任时才有用。

senses.title: Meticulous preparation
senses.definition: preparing so thoroughly that few surprises remain
senses.definitionCN: 准备得如此彻底，以致少有意外
senses.example: The meticulous preparation removed most of the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 周密的准备去掉了大部分风险。
senses.why: Preparation is a way of buying certainty with time.
senses.whyCN: 准备是用时间购买确定性的一种方式。

senses.title: Meticulous appearance
senses.definition: dressing and grooming with close attention
senses.definitionCN: 在穿着与修饰上极为留意
senses.example: His meticulous appearance suggested a careful mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲究的仪容暗示一颗谨慎的心。
senses.why: Appearance is a public record of private habits, so it can be read as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 仪容是私人习惯的公开记录，因此可以被当作证据来读。

senses.title: Meticulous attention
senses.definition: the act of watching something closely enough to catch small errors
senses.definitionCN: 足够贴近地观察以捕捉小错误
senses.example: A meticulous reading found the one wrong date.
senses.exampleCN: 一次细致的阅读找出了那个错误的日期。
senses.why: Most errors are small and quiet; only attention of this kind hears them.
senses.whyCN: 多数错误又小又安静；只有这种注意力能听见它们。

senses.title: Meticulous criticism
senses.definition: criticism that examines each small claim rather than the whole
senses.definitionCN: 逐一检查小主张而非整体的批评
senses.example: The review was meticulous and therefore slow to accept anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇评论细密，因此对任何东西都迟迟不肯接受。
senses.why: Examining every claim protects against error and can also paralyse.
senses.whyCN: 检查每个主张能防错，也能让人瘫痪。

senses.title: Meticulous but slow
senses.definition: the cost of detail: work that cannot be hurried
senses.definitionCN: 细节的代价：无法被催促的工作
senses.example: The meticulous method was right and three weeks late.
senses.exampleCN: 这套细致的方法是对的，但迟了三周。
senses.why: The word can turn critical when detail becomes the master rather than the servant.
senses.whyCN: 当细节成了主人而不是仆人，这个词就会转为批评。

senses.title: Meticulous honesty
senses.definition: a scrupulous accuracy about facts, including one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对事实的严谨准确，包括对自己
senses.example: He was meticulous even about his own mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 他甚至对自己的错误也一丝不苟。
senses.why: Honesty of this kind costs more, because it has no exception for the self.
senses.whyCN: 这种诚实代价更高，因为它对自我不设例外。

intro.en: Meticulous comes from a Latin word for fear, and its modern praise still carries a trace of anxiety.
intro.cn: meticulous 来自一个意为「恐惧」的拉丁词，它现代的赞美里仍带一丝焦虑。

items.en: Meticulosus meant fearful, timid, built from metus, fear.
items.cn: meticulosus 意为「胆怯的、畏缩的」，由 metus（恐惧）构成。

items.en: Metus means fear, dread, and also gives the rare English metus.
items.cn: metus 意为恐惧、畏惧，也给出英语中罕用的 metus。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 19c. with a new sense: careful to the point of anxiety.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用这个词，并赋予新义：仔细到近乎焦虑。

items.en: The meaning moved from frightened to scrupulous, because fear makes a person check twice.
items.cn: 意义从「害怕」移向「严谨」，因为恐惧会让人检查两遍。

items.en: Modern English uses it mostly as praise, though a hint of fussiness can remain.
items.cn: 现代英语多把它当赞美，尽管仍可能留一点挑剔的暗示。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fear root; the near-meaning group ranks degrees of care.
note.cn: 形近组共享「恐惧」词根；近义组排列仔细的程度。

entries.definition: with extreme care about detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节极度仔细地。

entries.definition: the quality of being very careful.
entries.definitionCN: 极其仔细的性质。

entries.definition: excessive attention to detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节的过度注意。

entries.definition: easily frightened.
entries.definitionCN: 容易受惊的。

entries.definition: very careful to be correct and fair.
entries.definitionCN: 极其小心以求正确公正的。

entries.definition: done with great and patient care.
entries.definitionCN: 以极大耐心细致完成的。

entries.definition: covering every part, leaving nothing out.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖每一部分、无所遗漏的。

entries.definition: very concerned about cleanliness or detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对洁净或细节极为在意的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of receipts aligned by date, size and colour before anyone asks.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「还没人要求，就把发票按日期、大小与颜色对齐」的画面。

normal.en: Meticulous comes from metus, fear: fear of a mistake is what makes the checking.
normal.cn: meticulous 出自 metus（恐惧）：怕出错，才去检查。

normal.en: Think of someone straightening a picture frame that is already straight.
normal.cn: 想象有人把已经挂正的画框再摆正一次。

normal.en: Say muh-TIK-yuh-lus; the tight middle sounds like a small adjustment.
normal.cn: 读成 muh-TIK-yuh-lus，紧促的中间音像一次微调。

normal.en: Link with timid: both begin in fear, but one ends in care.
normal.cn: 和 timid 联系：两者都始于恐惧，但一个终于细致。

normal.en: Pair it with detail: meticulous is detail with a nervous pulse.
normal.cn: 和 detail 配对：meticulous 是带着紧张脉搏的细节。

abstract.en: Care becomes a virtue when it serves the whole; it becomes a burden when it serves itself.
abstract.cn: 当细致服务于整体，它是美德；当它服务于自身，它是负担。

abstract.en: Checking twice is cheap compared with explaining once.
abstract.cn: 检查两遍比起解释一遍便宜。

abstract.en: The most careful people are often the ones who have seen what a small error costs.
abstract.cn: 最仔细的人，常常是见过小错误代价的人。

examples.en: His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
examples.cn: 他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。

examples.en: The clerk kept meticulous records of every delivery.
examples.cn: 这位职员对每次交付都做了精细记录。

examples.en: A meticulous reading found the one wrong date.
examples.cn: 一次细致的阅读找出了那个错误的日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: metic（怕）+ ulous（多……的）：怕出错而反复检查，就是「一丝不苟」。

root: 拉丁语 metus（恐惧）→ meticulosus（胆怯的），十九世纪转为「极其仔细」

sensesIntro.en: Meticulous is attention sharpened by worry; the senses differ in whether the worry serves accuracy, appearance or speed.
sensesIntro.cn: meticulous 是被担忧磨利的注意力；各义项的差别在于这担忧服务于准确、仪容，还是速度。

core.en: ATTENTION SHARPENED BY WORRY
core.cn: 被担忧磨利的注意力

branches.en: The core act: looking closely enough to catch what others miss.
branches.cn: 核心动作：看得足够近以捕捉他人所漏。

branches.en: Records and preparation built so nothing has to be redone.
branches.cn: 做到无需返工的记录与准备。

branches.en: Appearance and honesty kept at the same standard.
branches.cn: 以同一标准维系的仪容与诚实。

branches.en: The cost side: slowness and over-scrutiny.
branches.cn: 代价面：缓慢与过度审视。

branches.en: Detail as service versus detail as master.
branches.cn: 细节作仆人，与细节作主人。

intro.en: The metic family is small; the same Latin fear also gives timid, which shows where the word began.
intro.cn: metic 词族很小；同一个拉丁语「恐惧」也给出 timid，显示出这个词的起点。

latinIntro.en: Latin metus is fear, and meticulosus is full of it; the modern sense is what fear does to a person who must be right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metus 是恐惧，meticulosus 是充满恐惧；现代义就是恐惧对一个必须正确的人所做的事。

definition_zh: 节肢动物（身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的无脊椎动物）
definition_en: an invertebrate with a segmented body, a hard exoskeleton and jointed legs, such as an insect, spider or crab
core_image: 放大镜下一条分节的腿正在弯折，每个关节都像小小的折页铰链
scene: 放大镜下，观察者看见一条分节的腿在弯折，每一节都像小小的铰链。 The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint like a tiny hinge.
sceneCN: 这里 arthropod 指「节肢动物」（第 1 个义项：身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的动物）；句意为这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处像小铰链一样转动。

forms.label: 复合形容词（节肢动物传播的）

senses.title: A member of the phylum Arthropoda
senses.definition: any invertebrate of the phylum Arthropoda, with a segmented body and jointed appendages
senses.definitionCN: 节肢动物门中任何身体分节、附肢也分节的无脊椎动物
senses.example: The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处转动。
senses.why: The name is Greek for 'jointed foot', so the defining feature is written into the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字在希腊语里就是「分节的足」，因此定义特征直接写进了词里。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的节肢动物类群
senses.definition: the arthropods collectively, the largest animal phylum
senses.definitionCN: 所有节肢动物作为一个整体，是动物界最大的门
senses.example: Arthropods make up most known animal species.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物构成了已知动物物种的大多数。
senses.why: Because the group is enormous, the plural often stands for a category rather than a set of individuals.
senses.whyCN: 由于类群极庞大，复数形式常代表一个范畴，而不是若干个体。

senses.title: Used as an attributive label
senses.titleCN: 作定语标示传播或来源
senses.definition: used before another noun to say that something is carried, caused or made by arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示由节肢动物携带、引起或制造
senses.example: Arthropod-borne viruses spread faster in warm, wet seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的病毒在温暖潮湿的季节扩散更快。
senses.why: Public health needed a compact label for diseases carried by insects and ticks, and arthropod supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要简洁标签来指昆虫与蜱类携带的疾病，arthropod 正好补上。

senses.title: A fossil arthropod
senses.definition: ancient arthropod remains, including trilobites and fossil insects
senses.definitionCN: 古代节肢动物遗骸，包括三叶虫与昆虫化石
senses.example: Trilobites are arthropods that vanished before the dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫是在恐龙之前就灭绝的节肢动物。
senses.why: The hard exoskeleton fossilizes well, making arthropods central to palaeontology.
senses.whyCN: 硬外骨骼容易形成化石，使节肢动物成为古生物学的核心对象。

senses.title: An agricultural pest
senses.definition: an arthropod that damages crops or stored food
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物或仓储食物的节肢动物
senses.example: The spray targets arthropods that feed on the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这种喷剂针对取食叶片的节肢动物。
senses.why: Pest control needs a word broad enough to cover insects and mites together.
senses.whyCN: 害虫防治需要一个足够宽、能同时涵盖昆虫与螨类的词。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: an arthropod that transmits a pathogen from one host to another, such as a mosquito or tick
senses.definitionCN: 把病原体从一个宿主传给另一宿主的节肢动物，如蚊或蜱
senses.example: The mosquito is the arthropod responsible for the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是造成这次疫情的节肢动物媒介。
senses.why: Epidemiology uses the phylum name because the vector may be a fly, a flea or a tick.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学用门名，因为媒介可能是蝇、蚤或蜱。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: an arthropod used in genetics or physiology, especially the fruit fly
senses.definitionCN: 用于遗传学或生理学研究的节肢动物，尤指果蝇
senses.example: The fruit fly gave arthropods a central place in genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇让节肢动物在遗传学中占据了中心位置。
senses.why: Short generations and easy breeding made one arthropod the workhorse of genetics.
senses.whyCN: 世代短、易饲养，使某一种节肢动物成了遗传学的主力。

senses.title: An introduced or invasive species
senses.titleCN: 引入或入侵的节肢动物
senses.definition: an arthropod that has spread outside its native range and disrupts ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 扩散到原分布区之外、扰乱生态系统的节肢动物
senses.example: The introduced arthropod has no local predator.
senses.exampleCN: 这种外来节肢动物在当地没有天敌。
senses.why: Invasion biology names the group because the invader is often an insect or a crab.
senses.whyCN: 入侵生物学用类群名，因为入侵者常是昆虫或蟹类。

intro.en: Arthropod is Greek arthron 'joint' plus pous 'foot', a scientific compound that says exactly what the animal is. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: arthropod 由希腊 arthron「关节」加 pous「足」构成，这个科学复合词把动物的特征直接说了出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arthron meant 'joint, articulation'. It is generally connected to a root meaning 'to fit together', but that earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arthron 意为「关节、接合处」。一般认为它与意为「接合在一起」的词根有关，但那个更早的形式属重构。

items.en: Pous (stem pod-) meant 'foot', the same word behind tripod and podiatry.
items.cn: pous（词干 pod-）意为「足」，tripod 与 podiatry 也出自这个词。

items.en: The compound 'jointed foot' was coined in modern scientific Latin as Arthropoda and then borrowed into English as arthropod.
items.cn: 「分节的足」这一复合形式在近代科学拉丁语中被造为 Arthropoda，随后作为 arthropod 借入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century zoology fixed Arthropoda as the phylum containing insects, arachnids and crustaceans; the exact coiner and date are not settled.
items.cn: 19 世纪动物学把 Arthropoda 固定为包含昆虫、蛛形类与甲壳类的门；确切的造词者与年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century public health and agriculture produced fixed phrases such as arthropod vector and arthropod-borne disease.
items.cn: 20 世纪的公共卫生与农业产生了 arthropod vector、arthropod-borne disease 等固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Greek roots are clear, but the pre-Greek root of arthron is reconstructed and the exact first use of the English noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：希腊词根清楚，但 arthron 在希腊语之前的词根属重构，英语名词的确切首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek joint-root; group two holds animal-group names that overlap with arthropods without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「关节」词根的字词；第二组是与节肢动物重叠但并非同义的动物类群名。

entries.definition: Inflammation of a joint, built from arthron 'joint' plus -itis 'inflammation'; same root, medical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 关节炎症，由 arthron「关节」加 -itis「炎症」构成；同词根，医学义。

entries.definition: A joint or a joint disorder, from the same Greek root; it names a body part, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 指关节或关节病变，同出希腊词根；它指身体部位，不指动物。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'joint', used in arthroscopy and arthroplasty; it is a word part, not a whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「关节」的构词成分，用于 arthroscopy、arthroplasty；它是词素，不是完整单词。

entries.definition: The formal Latin name of the phylum; Arthropoda is the group, arthropod is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 该门的正式拉丁名；Arthropoda 是类群，arthropod 是其中一个成员。

entries.definition: A six-legged arthropod with three body regions; insects are a class inside Arthropoda, not the whole phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有六条腿、身体分三区的节肢动物；昆虫是节肢动物门内的一个纲，不是整个门。

entries.definition: An eight-legged arthropod such as a spider or tick; another class within the same phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有八条腿的节肢动物，如蜘蛛或蜱；同一门内的另一个纲。

entries.definition: A shelled arthropod such as a crab; it is a major subgroup of arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 有硬壳的节肢动物，如蟹；它是节肢动物的一个主要亚群。

entries.definition: Any animal without a backbone, including arthropods, mollusks and worms; it is broader than arthropod.
entries.definitionCN: 任何没有脊椎的动物，包括节肢动物、软体动物与蠕虫；比 arthropod 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arthro- 'joint' + pod 'foot': the animal with jointed feet.
normal.cn: arthro-「关节」+ pod「足」：长着分节足的动物。

normal.en: Insects, spiders, crabs and centipedes are all arthropods, but each is a different subgroup.
normal.cn: 昆虫、蜘蛛、蟹、蜈蚣都是节肢动物，但各属不同亚群。

normal.en: Arthropoda is the phylum; arthropod is one member of it.
normal.cn: Arthropoda 是门；arthropod 是门中的一个成员。

normal.en: Arthropod-borne disease is the fixed public-health phrase for infections carried by insects and ticks.
normal.cn: arthropod-borne disease 是公共卫生固定说法，指昆虫与蜱类携带的感染。

normal.en: The hard exoskeleton is why arthropods fossilize so well.
normal.cn: 硬外骨骼正是节肢动物容易形成化石的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a suit of armour worn outside the body, with every limb on a hinge.
abstract.cn: 想象一套穿在身体外面的盔甲，每条肢体都装在铰链上。

abstract.en: Picture a group so numerous that it outnumbers all other animals combined.
abstract.cn: 想象一个类群，数量超过其他所有动物的总和。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito that is both a pest and a delivery route for disease.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子，既是害虫，也是疾病的投送路径。

examples.en: Arthropods account for more than half of all described animal species.
examples.cn: 节肢动物占全部已描述动物物种的一半以上。

examples.en: The trap was designed to sample small arthropods in the soil.
examples.cn: 这个陷阱用来采集土壤中的小型节肢动物。

examples.en: Arthropod vectors include mosquitoes, fleas and ticks.
examples.cn: 节肢动物媒介包括蚊、蚤与蜱。

dict_mnemonic.text: arthro（关节）+ pod（足）——关节一节一节、足也一节一节，就是节肢动物

root: 希腊 arthron「关节」+ pous（词干 pod-）「足」；arthron 的更深词源一般认为是「接合」词根，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a jointed animal across disciplines: a phylum member, the vast group, a disease label, a fossil, a pest, a vector, a lab model and an invader.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种分节动物穿过不同学科：门类成员、庞大类群、疾病标签、化石、害虫、传播媒介、实验模型与入侵者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented leg bending at each joint like a row of tiny hinges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条分节的腿在每个关节处弯折，像一排小铰链。

branches.en: ONE AND ALL: a single jointed animal, or the largest phylum on Earth.
branches.cn: 个体与全部：单个分节动物，或地球上最大的门。

branches.en: CARRIER: the same group name labels diseases and names the vector.
branches.cn: 携带者：同一类群名既给疾病贴标签，也指传播媒介。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: hard exoskeletons make excellent fossils.
branches.cn: 深时：硬外骨骼极易形成化石。

branches.en: TROUBLE: the group includes both native pests and introduced invaders.
branches.cn: 麻烦：类群中既有本地害虫，也有外来入侵者。

branches.en: RESEARCH: short generations make one arthropod a genetic workhorse.
branches.cn: 研究：世代短，使某种节肢动物成为遗传学主力。

intro.en: Arthropod is a transparent Greek compound, and both halves recur in medical and scientific words.
intro.cn: arthropod 是透明的希腊复合词，两半都反复出现在医学与科学词汇中。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek, not Latin; arthron and pous entered scientific Latin as Arthropoda before English borrowed the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语；arthron 与 pous 先进入科学拉丁语构成 Arthropoda，英语再借入该名词。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出分节的身体。

items.example: The second element marks the limbs.
Every arthropod has a segmented body.
items.exampleCN: 每只节肢动物都有分节的身体。
节肢动物遍布每一处陆地生境。

items.example: The arthropodan cuticle is stiff but flexible.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物的角质层坚硬而有韧性。
节肢动物门是最大的门。

items.example: Arthritis shares the joint root but names a disease.
items.exampleCN: arthritis 同出「关节」词根，却指一种疾病。

items.example: Tripod uses the same foot word.

items.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的感染在夏季增多。

definition_zh: 与生俱来的权利；长子继承权；天生应得之物
definition_en: a right or privilege that you are entitled to at birth
core_image: 出生时握在掌心的一枚印章戒指
scene: 婴儿在摇篮里攥紧拳头，仿佛握着家训。 Education is every child's birthright.
sceneCN: 这里 birthright 是「与生俱来的权利」（第 2 个义项：人人都应享有的天赋权益）；句意是受教育是每个孩子生来就该拥有的权利。

pos.zh: 与生俱来的权利；长子继承权

collocations.phrase: the birthright of the eldest son

derivatives.zh: birth 加 day 的同构复合词，义为「生日」
birth 加 place 的同构复合词，义为「出生地」

senses.title: The special rights of the firstborn
senses.definition: the special rights or inheritance that belong to the firstborn son in a family
senses.definitionCN: 家庭中长子独有的继承权或特权
senses.example: Esau sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.
senses.exampleCN: 以扫为了一碗炖菜出卖了长子名分。
senses.why: In old law the first child held the estate, so the right was tied to the fact of being born first.
senses.whyCN: 旧时律法中长子承袭家业，这项权利与其出生次序直接绑定。

senses.title: A right you have from birth
senses.definition: a right or privilege that every person deserves simply by being born
senses.definitionCN: 仅因出生便应享有的权利或特权
senses.example: Education is every child's birthright.
senses.exampleCN: 受教育是每个孩子与生俱来的权利。
senses.why: What no one grants and no one may take away feels as if it were carried in from birth.
senses.whyCN: 非他人所赐也无人可夺的东西，仿佛自出生便已随身携带。

senses.title: A natural inheritance from one's origins
senses.titleCN: 承袭自出身的天赋或资产
senses.definition: a quality, talent, or heritage passed on by one's family or origins
senses.definitionCN: 由家庭或出身传递下来的品质、才能或遗产
senses.example: A feel for music was her birthright from a long line of players.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐天赋是她承袭自世代乐师之家的遗产。
senses.why: Qualities that run in the blood arrive before any effort, like rights granted at the cradle.
senses.whyCN: 流淌在血脉里的禀赋先于努力而来，如同在摇篮里便已授予。

senses.title: An entitlement wrongly given up
senses.titleCN: 被轻易舍弃的本应得之物
senses.definition: something so basic that trading it away is seen as a serious loss
senses.definitionCN: 根本到一旦被交换出去就构成重大损失的东西
senses.example: He traded his birthright of calm for a life of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 他用与生俱来的安宁换来了喧嚣的生活。
senses.why: Because a birthright is basic and unbargained, giving it up marks the trade as foolish.
senses.whyCN: 正因与生俱来的权利根本且不容议价，舍弃它便显得愚不可及。

senses.title: Citizenship granted by place of birth
senses.definition: legal citizenship obtained automatically through being born in a country
senses.definitionCN: 因出生在某国土地而自动获得的公民身份
senses.example: Birthright citizenship follows the soil, not the parents' papers.
senses.exampleCN: 出生公民权取决于出生地，而非父母的证件。
senses.why: If birth on the soil itself creates the right, that right is literally carried by the newborn.
senses.whyCN: 若出生地本身即创设权利，这权利便是新生儿落地即携带之物。

senses.title: The natural state one returns to
senses.definition: a natural condition, such as health or freedom, seen as one's due
senses.definitionCN: 被视为应得的自然状态，如健康或自由
senses.example: A good night's sleep felt like recovering a birthright.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜安眠仿佛赎回了本属于自己的一份权利。
senses.why: What the body or soul does by nature is felt as owed to it from the start.
senses.whyCN: 身心自然所向的状态，被感觉为从头便已欠给它的一份。

senses.title: The oldest claim in a lineage
senses.titleCN: 家族传承中最古老的主张
senses.definition: the oldest or primary claim within a family tradition or line
senses.definitionCN: 家族传统或世系中最古老、最根本的主张
senses.example: The eldest branch held the birthright to the family name.
senses.exampleCN: 长房一支握有家族姓氏的最初继承权。
senses.why: Lines of descent keep a ranking, and the earliest claim sits at the head.
senses.whyCN: 世系自有次序，最早的主张居于首位。

senses.title: Figurative inheritance of a group
senses.definition: a shared inheritance or defining feature of a people, place, or culture
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族、地方或文化共同承袭的财富或特质
senses.example: The old songs are the birthright of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这些古老歌谣是整片山谷共同的传承。
senses.why: A community passes on what defines it as if each member were born holding it.
senses.whyCN: 群体将其 defining 之物代代相传，仿佛每个成员生来便握在手中。

intro.en: Birthright is an Old English compound joining birth and right.
intro.cn: birthright 是古英语复合词，由 birth「出生」与 right「权利」拼合而成。

items.en: both parts are native Germanic words, with no Latin borrowing involved.
items.cn: 两个成分均为日耳曼本土词，不含拉丁借词。

items.en: gebyrtrihht and related forms named the privileges of rank one was born into.
items.cn: 古英语 gebyrtrihht 等形式指人生来所处的等级特权。

items.en: birthright appears in legal and biblical texts for the firstborn's share.
items.cn: 中古英语中 birthright 出现在法律与圣经文本中，指长子的名分。

items.en: the biblical story of Esau fixed the sense of a right that may be foolishly sold.
items.cn: 以扫的圣经故事固定了「可被愚妄出卖的权利」这一义。

items.en: the word widened to any right held from birth, including legal citizenship.
items.cn: 词义扩大为一切与生俱来的权利，包括法律上的出生公民权。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the birth- compound pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words for rights and inheritance.
note.cn: 形近组共享 birth- 复合模式；近义组汇集权利与继承类词。

entries.definition: the day of one's birth
entries.definitionCN: 生日——同为 birth 复合词，词义不同

entries.definition: the town where one was born
entries.definitionCN: 出生地——同为 birth 复合词

entries.definition: legal right to a creative work
entries.definitionCN: 版权——同含 -right，词源不同

entries.definition: property or qualities passed down
entries.definitionCN: 继承之物——偏财产与遗赠

entries.definition: a special right granted to some
entries.definitionCN: 特权——偏授予而非天生

entries.definition: a right guaranteed by law or rules
entries.definitionCN: 应得权益——偏制度赋予

normalIntro.en: Birthright joins birth and right, the right you carry from birth.
normalIntro.cn: birthright 由 birth 与 right 拼成，即生来携带的权利。

normal.en: Remember Esau selling his birthright for stew.
normal.cn: 记住以扫为一碗炖汤出卖长子名分的故事。

normal.en: It is one word, not birth right.
normal.cn: 它是一个词，不写作 birth right。

normal.en: The plural is birthrights.
normal.cn: 复数是 birthrights。

normal.en: Use it for rights, not for birthday parties.
normal.cn: 它指权利，不指生日派对。

normal.en: Law uses birthright citizenship today.
normal.cn: 当代法律用语有出生公民权。

abstract.en: See a newborn's hand closing around an invisible ring.
abstract.cn: 看新生儿的手攥住一枚看不见的印章戒指。

abstract.en: Feel the weight of something no one can hand you or take away.
abstract.cn: 感受那无人能赠予也无人能夺走之物的分量。

abstract.en: Picture a family seal pressed into wax at the cradle.
abstract.cn: 想象家族印章在摇篮边印进封蜡。

examples.en: Education is every child's birthright.
examples.cn: 受教育是每个孩子与生俱来的权利。

examples.en: Esau sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.
examples.cn: 以扫为了一碗炖菜出卖了长子名分。

examples.en: The old songs are the birthright of the whole valley.
examples.cn: 这些古老歌谣是整片山谷共同的传承。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不着来」——与生俱来的权利谁也夺不着、抢不来，出生就自带。

root: 日耳曼本土复合词：birth（古英语 gebyrd「出生」）+ right（古英语 riht「权利」）；中古英语定型为 birthright，指生来所属的等级特权与长子名分，后扩指一切与生俱来的权利。

sensesIntro.en: From the firstborn's legal share to every person's natural due, the word marks rights carried in from the cradle.
sensesIntro.cn: 从长子的法定名分到人人应得的自然权利，该词标记一切自摇篮便已携带的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal ring held in a newborn's palm
core.cn: 核心意象：新生儿掌心握着的印章戒指

branches.en: Rank and lineage claims
branches.cn: 等级与世系的主张

branches.en: Natural rights and states owed to all
branches.cn: 人人应得的自然权利与状态

branches.en: Qualities and heritage passed down
branches.cn: 承袭而来的品质与传承

branches.en: Rights foolishly traded away
branches.cn: 被愚妄舍弃的权利

branches.en: Citizenship by the soil
branches.cn: 依出生地取得的公民权

intro.en: Birthright is a native compound; its parts build many English words.
intro.cn: birthright 是本土复合词，其两个成分构出大量英语词。

latinIntro.en: Germanic compound pattern, with Latin cousins of right.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼复合模式，right 的拉丁同族词见下。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 直的；正当的（right 的远亲）

definition_zh: 地质构造的；地壳大尺度运动的；建筑构造的；（比喻）根本性的
definition_en: relating to the structure and large-scale movement of the Earth's crust, or to construction
core_image: 木匠把一根根木料搭成整体骨架，岩层也被巨大的力量搭成褶皱与断裂的骨架
scene: 古老海床被缓慢抬升，成了一片高原。 A tectonic uplift raised the ancient seabed into a plateau.
sceneCN: 这里 tectonic 指「地壳构造运动的」（第 1 个义项：与地壳大尺度变形有关的）；句意为一次构造抬升把古老海床抬成了一片高原。

pos.zh: 地质构造的；地壳运动的；建筑构造的；（比喻）根本性的

collocations.zh: 构造位移；（比喻）根本性转变

derivatives.zh: 构造作用；地壳构造运动

senses.title: Relating to crustal structure
senses.definition: relating to the structure and large-scale deformation of the Earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 与地壳的结构及大尺度变形有关的
senses.example: A tectonic uplift raised the ancient seabed into a plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 一次构造抬升把古老海床抬成了一片高原。
senses.why: The Greek root tekton means 'builder', so tectonic describes how the crust is built and rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 tekton 意为「建造者」，所以 tectonic 描述地壳如何被搭起与重建。

senses.title: Relating to plate motion
senses.definition: relating to the movement and interaction of lithospheric plates
senses.definitionCN: 与岩石圈板块的运动和相互作用有关的
senses.example: Tectonic plates carry continents thousands of kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 构造板块把大陆搬运数千公里。
senses.why: Once the crust is seen as built from plates, every plate interaction is a tectonic process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把地壳看作由板块搭成，每一次板块相互作用都是构造过程。

senses.title: Relating to mountain building
senses.definition: relating to the forces that raise mountain belts
senses.definitionCN: 与抬升山脉的那些力有关的
senses.example: The tectonic belt runs along the collision zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条构造带沿碰撞带延伸。
senses.why: Mountains are the visible result of crust being compressed and thickened, so the adjective covers the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 山脉是地壳受挤压增厚的可见结果，因此这个形容词覆盖整个造山过程。

senses.title: Relating to building or construction
senses.definition: relating to construction and the way a building is put together
senses.definitionCN: 与建造以及建筑如何组装有关的
senses.example: Architects study tectonic form, the visible logic of how a building is assembled.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师研究构造形式，即建筑如何组装的可见逻辑。
senses.why: This is the older sense: tekton is a carpenter or builder, and architecture inherited the word for the art of joining parts.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的义项：tekton 就是木匠或建造者，建筑学继承这个词，用来指拼接构件的技艺。

senses.title: A structural, far-reaching change
senses.titleCN: 比喻：结构性的、根本性的变化
senses.definition: used figuratively for changes that reshape the basic structure of something
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指重塑某事物基本结构的变化
senses.example: The internet caused a tectonic shift in how people shop.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网改变了人们购物的基本结构。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the scale of plate motion: slow, huge, and impossible to reverse once it starts.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了板块运动的尺度：缓慢、巨大，一旦开始就难以逆转。

senses.title: The adjective of tectonics
senses.definition: the adjective used in the names of subfields and processes of tectonics
senses.definitionCN: 用于构造学各分支与过程名称的形容词
senses.example: Tectonic studies combine field mapping with geophysics.
senses.exampleCN: 构造研究把野外填图与地球物理结合起来。
senses.why: Every discipline needs an adjective for its subject, so tectonic modifies studies, maps, models and events.
senses.whyCN: 每个学科都需要一个修饰其研究对象的形容词，于是 tectonic 修饰研究、图件、模型与事件。

senses.title: Visible construction logic in art
senses.definition: in art and design, describing the expressed logic of how parts support one another
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术与设计中，描述各部件如何相互支撑的可见逻辑
senses.example: The sculptor left the tectonic joints of the frame exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 雕塑家把框架的构造接点露在外面。
senses.why: A building shows its bones honestly when the joints are visible; critics borrowed tectonic for that honesty.
senses.whyCN: 当接点可见时，建筑就诚实地露出骨架；评论家借 tectonic 指这种诚实。

senses.title: Relating to structural earthquakes
senses.definition: describing earthquakes caused by crustal faulting rather than by volcanoes or collapse
senses.definitionCN: 描述由地壳断裂而非火山或塌陷引起的地震
senses.example: Most damaging quakes are tectonic rather than volcanic.
senses.exampleCN: 破坏性大的地震多是构造地震，而不是火山地震。
senses.why: Classifying a quake as tectonic is saying its cause is the building and breaking of the crust.
senses.whyCN: 把地震归为构造地震，就是说它的成因是地壳的搭建与破裂。

intro.en: Tectonic comes from Greek tekton 'builder, carpenter'. Architecture kept the older sense of construction, while geology took the word for the building of the crust. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tectonic 来自希腊语 tekton「建造者、木匠」。建筑学保留了「建造」的旧义，地质学则用这个词指地壳的搭建。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek tekton meant 'builder, carpenter, craftsman', and tektonike techne meant 'the art of building'; the verb tekein meant 'to build, produce'.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekton 意为「建造者、木匠、工匠」，tektonike techne 意为「建造的艺术」；动词 tekein 意为「建造、制作」。

items.en: Tektonikos meant 'skilled in building, relating to construction', which is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: tektonikos 意为「擅长建造的、与构造有关的」，是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Scientific Latin took tectonicus for structural descriptions, and European geology used it for the architecture of the crust.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语用 tectonicus 描述结构，欧洲地质学则用它指地壳的架构。

items.en: English geology adopted tectonic for the formation of folds, faults and mountain belts.
items.cn: 英语地质学采用 tectonic 指褶皱、断层与山脉带的形成。

items.en: Plate tectonics made the adjective everyday scientific vocabulary, and figurative uses such as tectonic shift spread into general speech.
items.cn: 板块构造学说使这个形容词成为常用科学词汇，而 tectonic shift 这类比喻用法也进入日常语言。

items.en: The deeper origin of tekein is reconstructed rather than attested; a common proposal links it to a root meaning 'to weave or fabricate'.
items.cn: tekein 的更早来源是重构而非有记录的；常见的一种假说把它连到一个意为「编织、制作」的词根上。

note.en: Group one holds words that differ from tectonic by a few sounds or letters; group two holds adjectives that also describe large-scale Earth structure.
note.cn: 第一组是与 tectonic 在读音或字母上只差一点的词；第二组是同样描述地球大尺度结构的形容词。

entries.definition: a technique or technical detail; it is built on the same Greek root but means skill, not crustal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 技巧或技术细节；它同出希腊词根，但指技能，不指地壳结构。

entries.definition: the field or process noun; tectonic is the adjective, tectonics the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 学科或过程名词；tectonic 是形容词，tectonics 是名词。

entries.definition: giving strength or tone; the first syllable is not tek- and there is no -nic ending.
entries.definitionCN: 起强壮或提振作用的；第一音节不是 tek-，也没有 -nic 结尾。

entries.definition: a plan for achieving something; it has /tæk/ at the start, not /tek/.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成目标而制定的策略；开头是 /tæk/ 而不是 /tek/。

entries.definition: relating to structure in any field; it is the neutral word, while tectonic is tied to the Earth's crust or to building.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何领域的结构有关；它是中性词，而 tectonic 专指地壳或建筑。

entries.definition: relating to geology as a whole, including rocks, fossils and time; tectonic is only the structural part.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地质学有关，包括岩石、化石与时间；tectonic 只涉及构造部分。

entries.definition: relating specifically to the crust; tectonic can involve the upper mantle as well.
entries.definitionCN: 专指地壳的；而 tectonic 也可涉及上地幔。

entries.definition: relating to mountain building; tectonic is wider and covers rifting and plate motion too.
entries.definitionCN: 专指造山的；tectonic 范围更广，也包括裂谷与板块运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real architectural links, so the word can be rebuilt from its parts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的建筑学关联，因此这个词可以从构件重建。

normal.en: tekton means builder, so tectonic is about how the Earth is built: plates, folds and faults.
normal.cn: tekton 表示建造者，所以 tectonic 讲的是地球如何被搭建：板块、褶皱与断层。

normal.en: Architecture uses tectonic for visible construction logic, which is the same root as geology's usage.
normal.cn: 建筑学用 tectonic 指可见的构造逻辑，这与地质学的用法同出一个词根。

normal.en: tectonic is the adjective and tectonics is the noun, just as economic pairs with economics.
normal.cn: tectonic 是形容词，tectonics 是名词，正如 economic 与 economics 的配对。

normal.en: A tectonic shift is slow and enormous, which is why the phrase works for social change.
normal.cn: 构造位移缓慢而巨大，所以这个短语也适用于社会变化。

normal.en: A tectonic earthquake comes from faulting, not from a volcano, so the label names the cause.
normal.cn: 构造地震来自断层活动而非火山，所以这个标签指的是成因。

abstract.en: Abstractly, tectonic means built and rebuilt: a structure is assembled, stressed, and then reassembled.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tectonic 表示搭建与重建：结构被组装、受力，然后重新组装。

abstract.en: The metaphor scales: a carpenter joins beams, the Earth joins plates, a society joins institutions, and all can shift.
abstract.cn: 这个比喻可以缩放：木匠拼接梁木，地球拼接板块，社会拼接制度，而它们都会位移。

abstract.en: Symbol: two arrows pressing a layered stack into folds, with a joint line where the layers meet.
abstract.cn: 符号：两个箭头把层叠的岩层压成褶皱，层与层相接处留一条接缝线。

examples.en: Tectonic forces built the mountain range over millions of years.
examples.cn: 构造力在数百万年间造就了这条山脉。

examples.en: The region is tectonically active and has many small earthquakes.
examples.cn: 该地区构造活动活跃，有许多小地震。

examples.en: The merger produced a tectonic change in the industry.
examples.cn: 这次合并使行业发生了根本性变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泰克托尼」—— 泰克是技术，托尼是木匠名，木匠搭骨架 → tectonic 构造的

root: 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者、木匠）及其形容词 tektonikos，核心含义是「与建造、构架有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tectonic. The core is construction: the crust is built into plates and folds, and buildings are built into visible frames.
sensesIntro.cn: tectonic 的八个义项。核心是「建造」：地壳被搭成板块与褶皱，建筑被搭成可见的骨架。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a builder joining parts into a frame, applied to rock layers and to buildings.
core.cn: 核心意象：建造者把构件拼成骨架，这一形象既用于岩层，也用于建筑。

branches.en: CRUST AS A FRAME: structure is the base meaning, and the adjective names the field.
branches.cn: 地壳即骨架：结构是基础义，这个形容词为这一领域命名。

branches.en: BUILDING THE EARTH: plates move, and their collisions raise mountains.
branches.cn: 建造地球：板块移动，板块碰撞抬起山脉。

branches.en: VISIBLE CONSTRUCTION: architecture and art keep the literal craft sense.
branches.cn: 可见的建造：建筑与艺术保留了字面上的工艺义。

branches.en: METAPHOR OF SCALE: slow, huge structural change borrows the image of moving plates.
branches.cn: 尺度的比喻：缓慢而巨大的结构变化借用了板块移动的形象。

branches.en: CAUSE LABEL: a tectonic earthquake is named for how the crust broke.
branches.cn: 成因标签：构造地震按地壳如何破裂来命名。

intro.en: Tectonic is built on a Greek root for building, with suffixes that turn it into a noun, an adverb and a field name.
intro.cn: tectonic 建立在希腊语「建造」词根上，后缀把它变成名词、副词与学科名称。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek tekton and tektonikos, loaned into scientific Latin as tectonicus. There is no separate Latin root family, so latinEntries stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语 tekton 与 tektonikos，后被借入科学拉丁语作 tectonicus。这里没有另一支拉丁词根族，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaning: one who builds or joins materials
items.example: The root names the craftsman, not the material.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指工匠，而不是材料。

items.meaning: relating to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a field name into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科名词变成描述性形容词。

items.meaning: the study or process of crustal structure
items.meaningCN: 研究地壳结构的学科或过程
items.example: Plate tectonics united geology in the nineteen sixties.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造学说在二十世纪六十年代统一了地质学。

items.example: The basin is tectonically quiet today.
items.exampleCN: 这个盆地今天构造活动平静。

items.example: Ancient tectonism folded the layers twice.
items.exampleCN: 古老的构造作用两次使岩层褶皱。

items.meaningCN: 研究地壳变形的物理学
items.example: Tectonophysics models stress in the crust.
items.exampleCN: 构造物理学对地壳中的应力建模。

items.meaning: a rigid piece of the lithosphere
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈的一块刚性板块
items.example: Each tectonic plate moves as one body.
items.exampleCN: 每个构造板块作为整体移动。

items.meaning: raising of the crust by tectonic forces
items.meaningCN: 由构造力引起的地壳抬升
items.example: Tectonic uplift exposed marine fossils high in the mountains.
items.exampleCN: 构造抬升把海洋化石暴露在高山上。

items.meaning: an earthquake caused by fault slip
items.meaningCN: 由断层滑动引起的地震
items.example: The tectonic earthquake damaged several villages.
items.exampleCN: 这次构造地震损坏了几个村庄。

definition_zh: 矩形的；长方形的；直角的
definition_en: shaped like a rectangle, or meeting at right angles
core_image: 砖窑里每一块砖都被切成长方形，码起来时边角严丝合缝
scene: 砖窑里的砖都被切成长方形，砌墙时边角对得整整齐齐。 The bricks were cut rectangular so that the wall would not wobble.
sceneCN: 这里 rectangular 指矩形的、长方形的（第 1 个义项：形状像矩形）；句意为砖被切成长方形，砌起来墙才不会晃。

pos.zh: 矩形的；长方形的；直角的

senses.title: A rectangular table
senses.definition: having the shape of a rectangle, with four straight sides and right angles
senses.definitionCN: 形状像矩形，有四条直边和直角
senses.example: The bricks were cut rectangular so that the wall would not wobble.
senses.exampleCN: 砖被切成长方形，砌起来墙才不会晃。
senses.why: The first sense is about outline: the object looks like a rectangle.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项讲的是外形：这件东西看起来像一个矩形。

senses.title: Rectangular coordinates
senses.definition: of lines or axes, meeting at right angles
senses.definitionCN: 指线或坐标轴以直角相交
senses.example: The plan uses rectangular coordinates for every corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图对每个角点都采用直角坐标。
senses.why: Here the word is about the angle, not the outline.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是角，而不是外形。

intro.en: Rectangular comes from Medieval Latin rectangularis, built on rectangulus, 'having right angles'.
intro.cn: rectangular 来自中世纪拉丁语 rectangularis，构词基础是 rectangulus（有直角的）。

items.en: Rectus meant straight or right.
items.cn: rectus 意为直的、正的。

items.en: Angulus meant a corner or an angle.
items.cn: angulus 意为角、拐角。

items.en: The compound meant right-angled.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为有直角的。

items.en: Medieval Latin added the adjective ending.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: English uses it for shapes and for axes.
items.cn: 英语用它说形状，也说坐标轴。

note.en: The look-alike group is the rect- family; the near-meaning group separates oblong, quadrangular, right-angled and boxy.
note.cn: 形近组是 rect 词族；近义组把「长方形的」「四角的」「直角的」「方盒状的」分开。

entries.definition: a figure with four right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 四个直角的图形。

entries.definition: the quality of being rectangular.
entries.definitionCN: 呈矩形的性质。

entries.definition: bounded by straight lines.
entries.definitionCN: 以直线为界的。

entries.definition: to correct or make straight.
entries.definitionCN: 纠正；弄直。

entries.definition: longer than it is wide.
entries.definitionCN: 长大于宽的。

entries.definition: having four angles.
entries.definitionCN: 有四个角的。

entries.definition: containing a right angle.
entries.definitionCN: 含有一个直角的。

entries.definition: square and block-like in shape.
entries.definitionCN: 方正而像盒子的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a brick wall where every brick is the same long block.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「每一块砖都是同一个长条块」的砖墙画面。

normal.en: Rectangular is rectangle plus the adjective ending.
normal.cn: rectangular 就是 rectangle 加上形容词词尾。

normal.en: Picture the corner where two walls meet at a perfect right angle.
normal.cn: 想象两面墙以完美的直角相交的那个角。

normal.en: Say rek-TANG-gyuh-ler; TANG carries the stress.
normal.cn: 读 rek-TANG-gyuh-ler，重音在 TANG。

normal.en: A brick is rectangular; a heap of bricks is not.
normal.cn: 一块砖是矩形的，一堆砖不是。

normal.en: The word also describes axes that cross at ninety degrees.
normal.cn: 这个词也描述以九十度相交的坐标轴。

abstract.en: Rectangular describes a promise that the corners will behave.
abstract.cn: rectangular 描述的是一种「角会守规矩」的承诺。

abstract.en: The adjective turns a shape into a rule for building.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词把一种形状变成了建造的规则。

abstract.en: Ordinary walls are rectangles that forgot they were geometry.
abstract.cn: 寻常的墙是忘了自己是几何的矩形。

examples.en: The bricks were cut rectangular so that the wall would not wobble.
examples.cn: 砖被切成长方形，砌起来墙才不会晃。

examples.en: A rectangular table stood against the far wall.
examples.cn: 一张长方形的桌子靠在对面的墙边。

examples.en: The plan uses rectangular coordinates for every corner.
examples.cn: 这张图对每个角点都采用直角坐标。

dict_mnemonic.text: rect（直）+ angular（有角的）→ 四个角都是直角的。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 rectangularis → rectus（直的）+ angulus（角）

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: an object whose outline is a rectangle, and lines that meet at right angles.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：外形是矩形的物体，以及以直角相交的线。

core.en: A BRICK THAT KEEPS ITS CORNERS
core.cn: 守住边角的砖

chain: THE AXES MEET AT RIGHT ANGLES

branches.en: An outline that looks like a rectangle.
branches.cn: 看起来像矩形的外形。

branches.en: Axes or lines crossing at right angles.
branches.cn: 以直角相交的坐标轴或直线。

branches.en: The shape and the angle share one root.
branches.cn: 形状与角共享同一个词根。

branches.en: Bricks, tables and fields take the shape.
branches.cn: 砖、桌子、田地取这种形状。

branches.en: Surveying and graphs take the angle.
branches.cn: 测量与图表取这个角。

intro.en: The rect- family is about straightness: rectangle, rectilinear, rectify and rectitude all stand on rectus.
intro.cn: rect 词族讲的是「直」：rectangle、rectilinear、rectify、rectitude 都立在 rectus 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin rectus and angulus combine into rectangulus; the adjective ending -aris turns the shape into a description.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rectus 与 angulus 合成 rectangulus；形容词词尾 -aris 把形状变成一种描述。

items.example: The beds were laid out rectangularly.

definition_zh: 情谊；同志情谊；同伴之间的友爱默契
definition_en: a feeling of mutual trust, loyalty, and good fellowship among people who spend time together
core_image: 一支球队赢球后互相撞肩大笑：一起流过汗的人之间那种不设防的亲近
scene: 加班到深夜的团队点了一桌外卖，边吃边笑，谁也没提明天。 The camaraderie in the unit carried them through the hardest month.
sceneCN: 这里 camaraderie 是「同事情谊」（第 1 个义项：共事者之间互信互助的情谊）；句意是团队里这份同袍情谊支撑他们熬过了最艰难的一个月。

pos.zh: 同志情谊；同伴间的友爱与默契

collocations.phrase: the camaraderie of the locker room

derivatives.zh: 同词源名词，义为「同伴；同志；战友」
由 comrade 加形容词后缀构成，义为「同志般的；友爱的」
由 comrade 加名词后缀构成，义为「同志情谊」，与 camaraderie 近义

senses.title: Good fellowship among people who work or train together
senses.titleCN: 共事者、同训者之间的情谊
senses.definition: mutual trust and easy friendliness that grows among teammates, colleagues, or soldiers through shared effort
senses.definitionCN: 在共同付出中于队友、同事或士兵之间生长出的互信与自然亲近
senses.example: The camaraderie of the rowing crew made the brutal training bearable.
senses.exampleCN: 赛艇队里的同袍情谊让严酷的训练变得可以忍受。
senses.why: The French source camarade means roommate in barracks, and shared quarters breed easy trust.
senses.whyCN: 法语词源 camarade 本指同住一间营房的人，同吃同住自然生出无戒备的信任。

senses.title: Loyalty produced by shared hardship
senses.definition: loyalty and solidarity forged by facing danger, hardship, or a common enemy together
senses.definitionCN: 因共同面对危险、艰苦或同一敌人而结成的忠诚与团结
senses.example: Survivors of the expedition still speak of their camaraderie with awe.
senses.exampleCN: 那次远征的幸存者至今谈起彼此间的情谊仍心存敬畏。
senses.why: Hardship strips away pretense, leaving only the plain fact of relying on each other.
senses.whyCN: 艰苦剥去了客套虚饰，只剩下彼此依靠这个朴素的事实。

senses.title: The warm atmosphere of a close group
senses.definition: the cheerful, unforced atmosphere of humor and goodwill inside a tight-knit group
senses.definitionCN: 紧密团体内部那种带笑意、不做作的融洽气氛
senses.example: There was real camaraderie in the newsroom on election night.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之夜，新闻编辑室里洋溢着真正的同事情谊。
senses.why: When trust is established, it becomes visible as shared jokes and ease rather than effort.
senses.whyCN: 信任一旦建立，就外化为 shared jokes 式的自如与轻松，而不需刻意维系。

senses.title: Spirit of collective effort
senses.titleCN: （为共同目标而）齐心协力的精神
senses.definition: the collective spirit that makes a group pull together toward a common goal
senses.definitionCN: 使一个团体为共同目标齐心协力的集体精神
senses.example: The volunteers worked with a camaraderie that impressed the organizers.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们齐心协力的劲头让组织者印象深刻。
senses.why: Shared purpose channels fellowship into joint action, the active face of the same bond.
senses.whyCN: 共同目标把情谊导入联合行动，是同一种纽带的能动一面。

intro.en: Camaraderie comes from French camarade, from Spanish camarada, roommate in barracks, ultimately from Latin camera, a vaulted room.
intro.cn: camaraderie 来自法语 camarade，再往前是西班牙语 camarada（同住营房者），最终可追溯到拉丁语 camera（拱顶房间）。

items.en: The root *kam- relates to bending or arching, the shape of early vaulted rooms.
items.cn: 词根 *kam- 与弯曲、拱形有关，正是早期拱顶房间的形状。

items.en: Latin camera meant a vaulted chamber, later a room generally; it also gives camera in optics.
items.cn: 拉丁语 camera 指拱顶密室，后泛指房间；光学上的「暗箱」camera 亦出于此。

items.en: Spanish camarada meant a company of soldiers sharing a room, then the roommates themselves.
items.cn: 西班牙语 camarada 指同住一室的班组士兵，继而指这些室友本身。

items.en: French borrowed it as camarade, comrade, and formed camaraderie for the spirit between such companions.
items.cn: 法语借为 camarade（同伴、同志），并派生 camaraderie 表示这类同伴之间的情谊。

items.en: English took camaraderie from French in the mid-nineteenth century; comrade had entered earlier by the same route.
items.cn: 英语于十九世纪中叶经法语借入 camaraderie；comrade 更早经同一渠道进入英语。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to teams, workplaces, and units, always with warmth and shared effort implied.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖团队、职场与部队，始终暗含温暖与共同付出。

note.en: Camaraderie is often misspelled by swapping its first syllables with those of comrade; the words are cousins, not identical.
note.cn: camaraderie 常因与 comrade 词头互换而被拼错；两者是表亲而非同一形式。

entries.definition: An Englished respelling of the same word, sometimes accepted but less standard.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英语化拼写变体，偶见使用但不够标准。

entries.definition: A companion or fellow member of a movement, the person behind the feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同伴、同志，是这种情谊背后的那个人。

entries.definition: A small secretive group of advisers; same Latin camera root but an ominous sense.
entries.definitionCN: 小密谋集团、私党；同出拉丁 camera 词根但含义阴暗。

entries.definition: The optical device, from the Latin word for vaulted room.
entries.definitionCN: 照相机，源自拉丁语「拱顶房间」一词。

entries.definition: Fellowship between comrades, nearly synonymous and plainer in style.
entries.definitionCN: 同志情谊，与 camaraderie 近乎同义，文风更朴素。

entries.definition: Friendly association and shared feeling within a group.
entries.definitionCN: 团体内的友好交往与共同情感。

entries.definition: Pride and loyalty binding a unit together, a French borrowing used for troops and teams.
entries.definitionCN: 团结精神、集体荣誉感，法语借词，多用于部队和团队。

entries.definition: Mutual understanding between two people, narrower than group camaraderie.
entries.definitionCN: 两人之间的默契融洽，范围比团体情谊窄。

entries.definition: The state of being alienated from former companions.
entries.definitionCN: 疏远、隔阂，是 camaraderie 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on the roommate-in-barracks origin and the comrade family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「同营房室友」词源与 comrade 词族的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root link: camarade, from Spanish camarada, meant soldiers sharing one barracks room.
normal.cn: 词根线索：camarade 源自西班牙语 camarada，本指同住一间营房的士兵。

normal.en: Family link: comrade and camaraderie share one Romance source, camera, a vaulted room.
normal.cn: 词族线索：comrade 与 camaraderie 同出罗曼语源 camera（拱顶房间）。

normal.en: Spelling guard: ca-ma-ra-de-rie keeps the order of camarade plus -rie; comradery swaps in the com-.
normal.cn: 拼写防守：ca-ma-ra-de-rie 即 camarade 加 -rie；comradery 才换成了 com- 词头。

normal.en: Collocation frame: a sense of camaraderie is the standard noun phrase in essays and exams.
normal.cn: 搭配框架：a sense of camaraderie 是文章与考试中的标准名词短语。

normal.en: Contrast word: rapport binds two people, camaraderie binds a whole group.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：rapport 连接两个人，camaraderie 凝聚一整群人。

abstract.en: One barracks room, sixteen bunks, and a silence that feels safe because everyone guards it together.
abstract.cn: 一间营房、十六张铺位，沉默也令人安心，因为所有人都共同守护着这份安稳。

abstract.en: A rowing shell: eight backs moving as one spine, no words needed.
abstract.cn: 一条赛艇：八个脊背如同一根脊柱起伏，无需言语。

abstract.en: Tents around one fire: the fire is the group, the warmth is the word.
abstract.cn: 围着同一堆篝火的帐篷：火堆是群体，暖意就是这个词。

examples.en: Years of camaraderie did not stop the two partners from disagreeing on strategy.
examples.cn: 多年的情谊并没有阻止两位合伙人在战略上产生分歧。

examples.en: New recruits quickly absorb the camaraderie of the squad.
examples.cn: 新兵很快就能融入班里的同袍情谊。

examples.en: Managers who fake camaraderie are quickly found out.
examples.cn: 假装与员工亲善的管理者很快就会被识破。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烤吗拉得热」——一队人围着火堆烤火，你问我火烤吗，我说拉过来烤得热乎点，围着火的这股热乎劲儿就是战友情、同伴情谊。

root: 经法语 camarade 上溯至西班牙语 camarada（同住一室的士兵班组），源自 cámara（房间），后者来自拉丁语 camera（拱顶房间），一般认为可再上溯至印欧词根 *kam-（弯曲、拱形）。由「同住一室的人」引申出「同志」comrade，再派生抽象名词 camaraderie，指同伴间的情谊。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from barracks-room fellowship to hardship-forged loyalty, group warmth, and collective effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从营房室友的情谊出发，延伸为共患难铸成的忠诚、团体的融洽氛围以及齐心协力的精神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strangers who share one room and one hardship until they guard each other like family.
core.cn: 核心意象：陌生人同住一间屋、共渡一场难，直到像家人一样互相守护。

branches.en: THE BARRACKS: everyday fellowship of people who live and work together.
branches.cn: 营房：同吃同住同做事的人之间的日常情谊。

branches.en: THE FRONT LINE: loyalty tempered by shared danger.
branches.cn: 前线：被共同危险淬炼出的忠诚。

branches.en: THE ROOM ITSELF: the atmosphere a bonded group breathes.
branches.cn: 房间本身：一个紧密团体呼吸其中的氛围。

branches.en: THE TASK: fellowship converted into joint muscle toward one goal.
branches.cn: 任务：情谊转化为朝同一目标发力的合力。

branches.en: THE TEST: what managers and coaches try, and fail, to manufacture.
branches.cn: 考验：管理者与教练刻意营造却常常失败的功课。

intro.en: Camaraderie is camarade plus the abstract-noun ending -erie, literally the quality of being a comrade.
intro.cn: camaraderie 由 camarade 加抽象名词后缀 -erie 构成，字面即「身为同伴的特质」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base camera, vaulted room, heads a wide family of words about rooms, chambers, and those who share them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 camera（拱顶房间）衍生出一个庞大的词族，涵盖房间、密室及同室之人。

我的同学（法语用例示意）

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的抽象名词后缀

items.structure: Englished form of the same Romance word
items.example: an old comrade from the war

items.meaning: a room, esp. an official one
items.meaningCN: 房间；议事厅（camera 的法语途径同源对偶词）

latinEntries.exampleCN: 宫廷的密室（拉丁语用例示意）

definition_zh: 面部表情；脸上显示情绪的神情
definition_en: the look on a person's face that shows emotion or intention
core_image: 一张脸像仪表盘，把内里的情绪显示在表面
scene: 演员没有台词，只靠一张脸完成整场戏，导演在排练后说： The facial expression carried the whole scene.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 1 个义项：面部呈现出的情绪状态）；句意为整场戏靠面部表情撑了起来。

senses.title: The look on a face that shows emotion
senses.definition: the visible state of a person's face that reveals a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部所显示、透露某种情感的外观状态
senses.example: Her facial expression told us she had won.
senses.exampleCN: 她的面部表情告诉我们她赢了。
senses.why: The phrase joins the surface of the face to the outward pressing of feeling, so it names feeling made visible on the face.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把脸的表面与情感的向外压出结合起来，因此命名的是在脸上变得可见的情感。

senses.title: The act of producing such a look
senses.definition: the activity of moving the face so as to show a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 通过脸部动作来显示情感的活动
senses.example: Facial expression is studied frame by frame in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室逐帧研究面部表情的产生。
senses.why: The same phrase can name the activity rather than the result, as when researchers measure how a look is produced.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语也可以命名活动而不是结果，例如研究者测量神情是如何产生的。

senses.title: A specific configuration
senses.definition: a particular arrangement of the features, such as a smile or a frown
senses.definitionCN: 五官的某种特定排列，如微笑或皱眉
senses.example: A raised eyebrow is a familiar facial expression.
senses.exampleCN: 扬眉是一种人们熟悉的面部表情。
senses.why: Once a look is repeatable, it becomes a named pattern that can be recognized across faces.
senses.whyCN: 当一种神情可以重复出现时，它就成为一个可跨面孔识别的命名模式。

senses.title: A measurable muscular pattern in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中可测量的肌肉模式
senses.definition: in psychology, a coordinated pattern of facial muscle activity that can be coded
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中可被编码的面部肌肉协同活动模式
senses.example: Researchers coded each facial expression by action unit.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者按动作单元对每一种面部表情进行编码。
senses.why: Psychology turned the visible look into a measurable event, so the phrase names a pattern of muscle activity.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把可见的神情变成可测量的事件，因此这个短语命名的是一种肌肉活动模式。

senses.title: A controlled display in acting
senses.definition: a deliberately shaped look used by an actor to convey a character's state
senses.definitionCN: 演员为传达角色状态而有意塑造的神情
senses.example: The actor rehearsed the facial expression in a mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 演员对着镜子练习这个面部表情。
senses.why: Performance treats the look as a craft object that can be practised, held and released on cue.
senses.whyCN: 表演把神情当作可练习、可保持、可按提示释放的手艺对象。

senses.title: A nonverbal signal in communication
senses.definition: a wordless signal that can support, qualify or contradict what is said
senses.definitionCN: 一种无词信号，可以支持、限定或反驳所说的话
senses.example: A facial expression can contradict the words being spoken.
senses.exampleCN: 面部表情可能与正在说的话相矛盾。
senses.why: In interaction the face sends a message of its own, which may agree or disagree with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 在互动中，脸发出自己的信息，可能与嗓音一致，也可能不一致。

senses.title: A clinical sign
senses.definition: in medicine, a look of the face that indicates a neurological or physical state
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指示神经或身体状态的面部外观
senses.example: A mask-like facial expression appeared early in the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病早期就出现了面具样的面部表情。
senses.why: Medicine reads the face as evidence, so a fixed or altered look becomes a sign of a condition.
senses.whyCN: 医学把脸当作证据来读，因此固定或改变的神情成为某种病状的征兆。

senses.title: A depicted look in portraiture
senses.definition: the look represented by an artist in a portrait or figure
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家在肖像或人物形象中再现的神情
senses.example: The portrait's facial expression is deliberately ambiguous.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像的面部表情被有意画得含混。
senses.why: Art represents a face rather than possessing one, so the phrase names a depicted look.
senses.whyCN: 艺术是再现一张脸而不是拥有一张脸，因此这个短语命名的是被描绘的神情。

intro.en: Facial expression joins two Latin-derived words: facial, from facies 'form, face', and expression, from exprimere 'to press out'. The compound is modern English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: facial expression 由两个源自拉丁语的词结合而成：facial 来自 facies「形状、脸」，expression 来自 exprimere「压出」。这一合成词属近代英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Facies meant 'form, appearance, face'. Its deeper origin is not established, and proposed links to a root for making or shaping are reconstructions.
items.cn: facies 意为「形状、外观、脸」。其更深来源未得到证明，把它系于某个表示「制作、塑形」的词根只是重构。

items.en: The adjective facialis 'of the face' was formed from facies and entered English through French.
items.cn: 形容词 facialis「脸的」由 facies 构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Expression descends from exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'.
items.cn: expression 源自 exprimere「压出、表现」，由表示「向外」的前缀与表示「压」的词根构成。

items.en: The phrase facial expression became common in the eighteenth century, when physiognomy and portraiture paid close attention to the readable face.
items.cn: facial expression 这一短语在十八世纪变得常见，当时相面术与肖像画都密切关注可读的脸。

items.en: In the twentieth century psychology and medicine turned the phrase into a technical label for measurable or diagnostic facial patterns.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，心理学与医学把这个短语变成可测量或可诊断的面部模式的技术标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origins of facies and premere remain unsettled; proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个合成词确切的最早书证没有定论，facies 与 premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定，提出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and close morphological relatives of the phrase; group two holds near synonyms for the look of a face.
note.cn: 第一组是这个短语的组成部分与构词近亲；第二组是表示脸部外观的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective alone means 'of the face' and can describe nerves, features or treatments, not only expressions.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词单独使用时意为「脸的」，可描述神经、五官或护理，不只描述表情。

entries.definition: A medical term for the characteristic appearance of the face, often used in diagnosis; it is the Latin source of facial.
entries.definitionCN: 指面部特征性外观的医学术语，常用于诊断；它是 facial 的拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: The everyday English noun for the front of the head, which came through French from the same Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 指头部正面的日常英语名词，经法语来自同一拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean any act of showing feeling, a phrase or a mathematical formula; the compound narrows it to the face.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时可以指任何表达情感的行为、词语或数学式；合成后收窄到脸。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of the face; the compound adds the idea that the look reveals feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；这个合成短语多出「神情透露情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A literary word for the face and its expression, often suggesting composure or character.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸及其表情的文学用词，常暗示镇定或品格。

entries.definition: A formal or literary word for a face, especially its appearance; it does not focus on the emotion shown.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸、尤其是其外观的正式或文学用词；不聚焦于所显示的情绪。

entries.definition: The study or appearance of facial features as signs of character; the compound is about momentary feeling, not permanent character.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或指面部特征作为性格标志；这个合成短语讲的是短暂情绪，而不是持久性格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the face word, the expression word, the research use and the stage use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「脸」的词、「表达」的词、研究用法与舞台用法。

normal.en: The first word means 'of the face', the second means 'a showing', so the phrase is a showing on the face.
normal.cn: 第一个词意为「脸的」，第二个词意为「显示」，因此整个短语就是「脸上的显示」。

normal.en: The face has a small set of reusable patterns: smile, frown, raised brow, blank stare.
normal.cn: 脸有一套可重复使用的小模式：微笑、皱眉、扬眉、空白凝视。

normal.en: Research use: psychologists code the look muscle by muscle.
normal.cn: 研究用法：心理学家把神情一块肌肉一块肌肉地编码。

normal.en: Stage use: an actor can hold a look through a long silent shot.
normal.cn: 舞台用法：演员能在漫长的无声镜头里保持一种神情。

normal.en: Medical use: a fixed, mask-like look can be a sign of illness.
normal.cn: 医学用法：固定、面具般的神情可能是疾病的征兆。

abstract.en: Picture a face as a dashboard where each feeling lights a different lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象脸是一块仪表盘，每种情绪点亮不同的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait that keeps a secret by refusing to settle into one look.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像拒绝固定成一种神情，从而守住一个秘密。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that disagrees with the sentence being spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一个微笑与正在说出的句子互相矛盾。

examples.en: The interviewer noted his neutral facial expression and calm voice.
examples.cn: 面试官注意到他中性的面部表情与平静的嗓音。

examples.en: Software can now recognize a facial expression in a crowd.
examples.cn: 软件如今能在人群里识别面部表情。

examples.en: Her facial expression softened as the child ran toward her.
examples.cn: 孩子朝她跑来时，她的面部表情柔和下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脸部的」加「表达」——脸把情绪表达出来 → 面部表情

root: facial 来自拉丁语 facies「形状、脸」的形容词 facialis；expression 来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出」。短语为近代英语合成；facies 与 premere 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the visible look to the act that produces it, then to a named pattern, a measured muscle event, a stage craft, a signal, a symptom and a painted image.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从可见的神情，走到产生它的行为，再到命名的模式、被测量的肌肉事件、舞台手艺、信号、症状与画中的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the face as a surface where an inner state becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：脸是一块让内在状态变得可见的表面。

branches.en: LOOK AND MAKING THE LOOK: the visible state and the activity that produces it are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 神情与造出神情：可见状态与产生它的活动是同一事件的两面。

branches.en: NAMED PATTERN: a repeatable arrangement such as a smile becomes a recognizable unit.
branches.cn: 命名模式：像微笑这样可重复的排列成为一个可识别的单位。

branches.en: MEASURED AND DIAGNOSTIC: the same look can be coded as muscle activity or read as a medical sign.
branches.cn: 测量与诊断：同一神情既可被编码为肌肉活动，也可被读作医学体征。

branches.en: MADE AND DEPICTED: an actor shapes a look, and a painter represents one.
branches.cn: 塑造与描绘：演员塑造神情，画家再现神情。

branches.en: SIGNAL: the face sends a message that may support or contradict the voice.
branches.cn: 信号：脸发出的信息可以支持嗓音，也可以与之矛盾。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a face adjective and an expression noun, and both halves bring their own Latin relatives into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个表示「脸」的形容词与一个表示「表达」的名词构成，两半都各自带着拉丁语亲属进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin facies 'face' gives facial and facies; exprimere 'press out' gives expression and expressive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facies「脸」衍生 facial 与 facies；exprimere「压出」衍生 expression 与 expressive。

items.example: The Latin noun names the whole visible form.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词命名整个可见的形状。

items.example: The adjective entered English as facial.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词作为独立词进入英语。

items.example: The suffix marks relation to the face.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记与脸的关系。

items.example: A facial nerve controls the muscles of the look.
items.exampleCN: 面部神经控制神情所用的肌肉。
这对双胞胎在面部上相似。

items.example: The expression on her face changed first.
He has a highly expressive face.
items.exampleCN: 他有一张表情非常丰富的脸。

items.example: The software reads facial expression in real time.
items.exampleCN: 软件实时读取面部表情。

items.example: Facial recognition is a different task from expression analysis.
items.exampleCN: 人脸识别与表情分析是不同的任务。

definition_zh: 尽管；虽然；尽管如此
definition_en: in spite of; used as a preposition, a conjunction or a trailing adverb to say that something does not prevent the rest
core_image: 堤坝被水漫过一半，却仍然立在那里挡住洪水
scene: 连日暴雨，桥基泡在水里，工程队还是按时完成了加固。 Notwithstanding the heavy rain, the crew finished the reinforcement on schedule.
sceneCN: 这里指暴雨并未阻止施工（第 1 个义项：介词用法，后接名词表让步）；句意为尽管连日暴雨，工程队仍按时完成了加固。

pos.zh: 尽管（后接名词或名词短语）
尽管如此（放句末或独立使用）

collocations.zh: 尽管有任何相反约定（法律）

forms.label: 介词/连词/副词（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 经受住；抵挡（本词的构词核心）
withstand 的过去式与过去分词
withstand 的现在分词（本词的第二成分）
尽管（后接从句的固定形式）
排除性条款（法律中可排除其他规定的条款）

senses.title: The preposition before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase to say that it does not block what follows
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词短语前，表示它并不能阻挡后文所述
senses.example: Notwithstanding the rain, the match continued.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，比赛仍继续进行。
senses.why: The word began as a participle phrase meaning not withstanding, that is, not resisting, and it still carries that image of something standing up against pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是分词短语，意为「不抵挡」，即不因压力而退让，至今仍带着「顶住压力站着」的意象。

senses.title: The conjunction with that
senses.titleCN: 连词用法：后接完整从句
senses.definition: used with that to introduce a full clause of concession
senses.definitionCN: 后接连接词，引出完整的让步从句
senses.example: Notwithstanding that the evidence was thin, the case proceeded.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管证据薄弱，案件仍继续审理。
senses.why: Adding that turns the participle into a clause opener, which is the most formal way to concede a whole statement.
senses.whyCN: 后接连接词就把分词变成从句引导词，这是承认整句陈述最正式的方式。

senses.title: The trailing adverb
senses.definition: placed at the end of a clause to mean all the same
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句末尾，表示「仍然如此」
senses.example: The weather was bad; the match went on notwithstanding.
senses.exampleCN: 天气很糟，比赛还是照常进行。
senses.why: At the end of a clause the participle stands alone and repeats the concession already made by the facts.
senses.whyCN: 放在从句末尾时，这个分词独自站住，把事实已经作出的让步再说一遍。

senses.title: The postposition after a noun
senses.definition: placed after a noun instead of before it, a formal stylistic option
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词之后而非之前，是正式文体的一种选择
senses.example: The delays notwithstanding, the bridge opened on time.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有延误，这座桥仍按时通车。
senses.why: Because the word is historically a participle, it can follow its noun, as absolute constructions often do.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词历史上是分词，所以它能跟在名词之后，正如绝对结构常做的那样。

senses.title: The legal override clause
senses.definition: used in statutes and contracts to give a provision priority over others
senses.definitionCN: 在法条与合同中使某条款优先于其他规定
senses.example: Notwithstanding any other provision, this clause prevails.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有任何其他规定，本条仍然优先适用。
senses.why: Legally the word does not merely concede a fact; it cancels a competing rule, which is the strongest use of the image.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，这个词不只是承认一个事实，而是取消一条竞争性规则，这是该意象最强的用法。

senses.title: Not held back by a circumstance
senses.definition: used of a person or thing that is not limited by a stated factor
senses.definitionCN: 指人或事物不为所述因素所限
senses.example: Notwithstanding his age, he works full days.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管年事已高，他仍整日工作。
senses.why: The original sense of withstanding survives here: the factor presses, and the subject simply does not give way.
senses.whyCN: withstand 的原义在此存活：那个因素在施压，而主体就是不退让。

senses.title: Priority over an earlier agreement
senses.definition: used in contracts so that a term applies even where an earlier term says otherwise
senses.definitionCN: 用于合同，使某一条款即使在先条款另有规定时仍适用
senses.example: The clause applies notwithstanding the earlier agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有在先协议，本条款仍然适用。
senses.why: Hierarchy among clauses needs an explicit marker, and this is the marker that says the newer rule stands.
senses.whyCN: 条款之间的层级需要一个明确标记，而这个词正是说明新规则站得住的标记。

senses.title: The most formal concession
senses.definition: used where the register must be maximally formal, as in statutes and treaties
senses.definitionCN: 用于语体必须最正式的场合，如法条与条约
senses.example: Notwithstanding repeated warnings, the practice continued.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管一再警告，这种做法仍然继续。
senses.why: Because the word is long and archaic in shape, it suits documents that want weight rather than ease.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词形长而古，适合那些要分量而非轻便的文件。

intro.en: Notwithstanding is not plus withstanding, the participle of withstand, from Old English withstandan, to stand against. It is Germanic with no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; the legal non obstante is a counterpart only.
intro.cn: notwithstanding 是 not 加 withstanding，后者是 withstand 的分词；withstand 出自古英语 withstandan「站着对抗」。它属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；法律拉丁语 non obstante 只是对应说法。

items.en: Withstandan joins with, against, and standan, to stand: to stand against something pressing.
items.cn: withstandan 由 with「对抗」与 standan「站立」合成：顶着压力站着。

items.en: The participle withstanding appears in the sense of resisting, and the negative phrase not withstanding is built on it.
items.cn: 分词 withstanding 以「抵抗」之义出现，否定短语 not withstanding 便建在它上面。

items.en: Not withstanding comes to mean in spite of and is written as one word in legal and parliamentary records.
items.cn: not withstanding 转义为「尽管」，并在法律与议会记录中写成一个词。

items.en: The notwithstanding clause becomes a named constitutional device in Canadian law in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 在加拿大法律中，notwithstanding clause 于二十世纪成为一个有专门名称的宪法机制。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word for formal and legal prose; speech prefers despite or in spite of.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词留给正式与法律文字；口语更爱用 despite 或 in spite of。

note.en: The first group shares the withstand standing-root. The second group names concession at different weights, from the everyday to the legal.
note.cn: 第一组共享 withstand「顶住」词根。第二组按分量的轻重给出让步说法，从日常到法律。

entries.definition: To resist or endure pressure without giving way.
entries.definitionCN: 顶住压力而不退让。

entries.definition: The past and past participle of withstand.
entries.definitionCN: withstand 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: The participle inside the word, meaning resisting.
entries.definitionCN: 词内的分词成分，意为抵挡。

entries.definition: The conjunction form that takes a full clause.
entries.definitionCN: 接完整从句的连词形式。

entries.definition: A provision that lets a law override other rules, named in Canadian constitutional law.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某项法律排除其他规则的条款，加拿大宪法中有专名。

entries.definition: In spite of, with a noun or gerund; shorter and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管，后接名词或动名词；更短、更不正式。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the same relation.
entries.definitionCN: 表达同一关系的日常短语。

entries.definition: Concedes with a full clause, neutral in register.
entries.definitionCN: 用完整从句让步，语体中性。

entries.definition: All the same; marks the main clause as unaffected by what came before.
entries.definitionCN: 仍然如此；标出主句不受前文影响。

entries.definition: Without being affected by the stated factor.
entries.definitionCN: 不受所述因素影响。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real withstand standing-root and the real legal override clause.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 withstand「顶住」词根与真实的法律排除条款。

normal.en: Withstand is with plus stand: something stands against the pressure and does not fall.
normal.cn: withstand 是 with 加 stand：某物顶住压力站着，没有倒下。

normal.en: Not withstanding therefore means not giving way to, and the concession follows naturally.
normal.cn: not withstanding 因此意为「不向它退让」，让步义便自然跟出。

normal.en: The noun can come first: the delays notwithstanding, the bridge opened.
normal.cn: 名词可以放前面：尽管有延误，桥还是通车了。

normal.en: Statutes use notwithstanding to cancel a competing rule, not merely to admit a fact.
normal.cn: 法条用 notwithstanding 取消竞争性规则，而不只是承认事实。

normal.en: Despite is the everyday cousin; notwithstanding wears the formal coat.
normal.cn: despite 是日常表亲；notwithstanding 穿的是正式外套。

abstract.en: A dam holds even when the water is already halfway up its face.
abstract.cn: 堤坝即使水已漫到半腰，也仍然立着。

abstract.en: The word honours the thing that refuses to move, then lets the sentence move anyway.
abstract.cn: 这个词先致敬那个不肯让位的东西，然后让句子照样往前走。

abstract.en: Legal weight is a kind of weather that documents are built to stand in.
abstract.cn: 法律的分量是一种天气，而文件正是为站在这种天气里而造。

examples.en: Notwithstanding the cost, the repairs were approved.
examples.cn: 尽管成本高昂，修缮仍获批准。

examples.en: The committee proceeded notwithstanding that two members were absent.
examples.cn: 尽管两名成员缺席，委员会仍继续推进。

examples.en: The evidence was thin; the case went ahead notwithstanding.
examples.cn: 证据薄弱，案件却照旧进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「诺特维兹斯坦丁」，withstand 是「顶住」：not 加顶住，就是不被它挡住，即尽管

root: 古英语 withstandan「站着对抗」= with「对抗」+ standan「站立」→ 分词 withstanding → 否定短语 not withstanding「不向它退让」→ 十五世纪合为一词，义为「尽管」，可作介词、连词（notwithstanding that）与句末副词，也能后置在名词之后。属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词，latinEntries 留空；法律拉丁语 non obstante 只是对应说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one stance: something presses, and the main statement stands anyway. The word changes position and weight, from a preposition to a clause opener, a trailing adverb, a postposed phrase, and finally the heaviest legal override.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保持同一个姿态：有东西在施压，而主句照样站住。这个词改变的是位置与分量，从介词到从句引导词、句末副词、后置短语，最后到最重的法律排除用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dam already half overtopped, still holding the flood back.
core.cn: 核心意象：堤坝已被水漫过一半，却仍挡住洪水。

branches.en: NOT GIVING WAY: a noun phrase that does not block the result, and a person not limited by a factor.
branches.cn: 不退让：挡不住结果的名词短语，以及不受某因素限制的人。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE: notwithstanding that, the most formal way to concede a whole statement.
branches.cn: 从句：notwithstanding that，承认整句陈述最正式的方式。

branches.en: THE TRAILING WORD: standing alone at the end, repeating the concession.
branches.cn: 句末词：独自站在末尾，把让步再说一遍。

branches.en: THE POSTPOSED PHRASE: the participle following its noun, as absolute constructions do.
branches.cn: 后置短语：分词跟在名词之后，如绝对结构所为。

branches.en: THE OVERRIDE: cancelling a competing rule, giving priority to a later term, and the heaviest register.
branches.cn: 排除：取消竞争规则、使后订条款优先，以及最重的语体。

intro.en: Notwithstanding is a negative phrase built on the participle withstanding, which comes from withstand, itself with plus stand. No suffix is involved, so the items list components and parallel forms.
intro.cn: notwithstanding 是建在分词 withstanding 上的否定短语，而 withstanding 出自 withstand，即 with 加 stand。这里没有后缀，因此下面列出构词成分与平行形式。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; non obstante expresses the same legal move in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语 non obstante 表达同样的法律动作。

items.example: In withstand the first element means against, not together.
items.exampleCN: 在 withstand 里，第一个成分意为「对抗」，而不是「共同」。

items.example: Standing is the image the whole word keeps.
The verb names the act of not giving way.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「不退让」的动作。

items.example: The participle supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供复合词的后半截。

items.example: The negative turns resisting into not resisting.
items.exampleCN: 否定词把「抵挡」变成「不抵挡」。

items.structure: English compound phrase, fixed as one word
items.example: Legal records fix the single-word form in the fifteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 法律记录在十五世纪把它固定为单词形式。

items.example: The added that lets a full clause follow.
items.exampleCN: 加上 that 就能接完整从句。

items.example: Canadian constitutional law gives the device its name.
items.exampleCN: 加拿大宪法给了这一机制专名。

items.example: It is the shorter everyday alternative.
items.exampleCN: 它是更短的日常替代词。

items.example: It marks the clause that remains unaffected.
items.exampleCN: 它标记那个不受影响的主句。

definition_zh: 熔岩；熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石；熔岩穹丘；熔岩管；枕状熔岩；比喻大量涌出之物；熔岩灯
definition_en: molten rock that has reached a planet's surface and flows from a volcano, or the solid rock it forms when it cools
core_image: 火山口边缘，暗红的黏稠流体沿斜坡推进，表面结出黑色硬壳，壳缝里透出橙色光
scene: 夜里的山坡上，暗红色流体一边移动一边结壳，缓慢逼近远处的房屋。 A river of lava cut across the road and reached the sea by dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 lava 指流出地表的熔岩（第 1 个义项：到达地表并正在流动的高温熔融岩石）；句意为一条熔岩流横穿公路，天亮时抵达海边。

pos.zh: 熔岩（到达地表的熔融岩石）
熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石
熔岩灯；（比喻）大量涌出之物

derivatives.zh: 熔岩的；似熔岩的（较少见，地质学用）
熔岩般的；像熔岩那样炽热流动的
熔岩流（复合术语，指流动的熔岩体及其堆积）
